item.dc:creator: Stephen Douglas
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers had the night off on Monday. Multiple players took advantage by catching a a game at SoFi Stadium. Tarik Skubal and Mookie Betts were both in attendance on Monday as the Los Angeles Rams beat the New York Giants, 28-6. The Dodgers’ stars did not appear to be there together and had very different experiences. While Skubal was field level, Betts was up in the suites hanging out with Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald’s wife. While Betts was shown in a suite during the broadcast
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers had the night off on Monday. Multiple players took advantage by catching a a game at SoFi Stadium. Tarik Skubal and Mookie Betts were both in attendance on Monday as the Los Angeles Rams beat the New York Giants, 28-6. The Dodgers’ stars did not appear to be there together and had very different experiences.
While Skubal was field level, Betts was up in the suites hanging out with Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald’s wife.
While Betts was shown in a suite during the broadcast, Skubal was field level. The pitcher chatted with Rams’ tight end Colby Parkinson ahead of the game and posted pictures and video on Instagram. Blake Snell obviously wasn’t invited as he posted, “You think you know a guy… then he goes to the rams game solo… @tarikskubal,”on Skubal’s post.
Tarik Skubal attends first Rams game
— diem (@teohtani) September 22, 2026
The timing of Skubal attending the Rams game is interesting because of his current status with the team. On Sunday the Dodgers placed Skubal on the bereavement list saying the pitcher would be away from the team for a couple days. According to manager Dave Roberts he had, “Some personal stuff going on, but he’s fine.” Snell was probably just doing some gentle ribbing.
So it also makes sense that Skubal and Betts probably had no clue the other was there.
Mookie Betts, Myles Garrett and Erica Donald
Mookie Betts is spending his off day in a box with Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald's wife Erica pic.twitter.com/uSclGhb9zh
— Talkin' Baseball (@TalkinBaseball_) September 22, 2026
The Dodgers clinched the NL West last week. They have six games remaining on the schedule and Skubal is currently penciled in to start the final game of the regular season against the San Francisco Giants. It seems unlikely he makes that start for a number of reasons.

item.title: [mlb.com] Our final MVP poll has clear frontrunners, but can this week change anything?
item.dc:creator: Brian Murphy
item.description: As we make our way through the final week of the regular season, there doesn't seem to be much suspense as to who will be named MVP. At least, that's what we can glean from our latest -- and final -- MLB.com 2026 MVP poll. Yordan Alvarez is still well out in front in the American League despite relatively mediocre production of late. In the National League, Pete Crow-Armstrong is wrapping up one of the best all-around seasons in recent memory. Thirty-eight MLB.com experts cast votes for who they
item.content:encoded:
As we make our way through the final week of the regular season, there doesn't seem to be much suspense as to who will be named MVP. At least, that's what we can glean from our latest -- and final -- MLB.com 2026 MVP poll.
Yordan Alvarez is still well out in front in the American League despite relatively mediocre production of late. In the National League, Pete Crow-Armstrong is wrapping up one of the best all-around seasons in recent memory.
Thirty-eight MLB.com experts cast votes for who they think will earn MVP honors after this season, with 32 players receiving at least one vote. As a reminder, votes were based not only on results so far, but also on how things are expected to play out the rest of the season.
Voters ranked their top five picks in each league on a 5-4-3-2-1 scale -- five points for a first-place vote, four points for a second-place vote and so on. Here are the results.
All stats are through Sunday unless otherwise noted.
AMERICAN LEAGUE
Alvarez has been so good this year that what qualifies as a slump for him would be a good stretch for most other hitters. Over his past 41 games, he is hitting .264 with an .840 OPS. Again, not bad for most, but well below the standard of the AL leader in average (.313) and OPS (1.027). Alvarez has three homers and five RBIs through 16 games this month, leaving him tied with the O's Pete Alonso and one home run behind the Rays' Junior Caminero for the AL lead and nine RBIs behind Alonso for the top spot in that statistic. Even though his Triple Crown chances have faded, Alvarez has still put together an awesome 2026 at the plate. His 179 wRC+ is at least 27 points better than any other qualified hitter.
We know Caminero is one of the game's great sluggers. He is finishing up his second straight 40-homer season and swings harder than anyone. But what's been most impressive about his season is his improved strike-zone judgment. He has upped his walk rate from a below-average 6.3% to 11.5%, which ranks in the 80th percentile of MLB. He's also maintained a very solid strikeout rate (18.5%). He's not chasing as much, has shaved his whiff rate and is making more contact overall. That blend of patience, power and bat control is a special combination, especially in a 23-year-old player. Carrying a .363 on-base percentage (52 points better than last season), Caminero's .892 OPS ranks third in the AL.
Witt has had better offensive seasons, although 18 homers, 43 steals and a 119 wRC+ in 137 games is not too shabby. But when you consider his entire skill set, Witt remains extremely valuable. His +16 fielding run value is tied for third in the Majors, and his 22 outs above average tops the AL. He also has a +8 baserunning run value, one behind the D-backs' Corbin Carroll for the MLB lead. So while he hasn't been as undeniable in the batter's box as he was in 2024 (169 wRC+), Witt's all-around greatness has him atop the AL FanGraphs WAR leaderboard (6.6) and in line for a possible top-five finish in the MVP voting for the third time in three years.
There has been quite a bit of MVP chatter surrounding Schlittler in recent weeks. And why not? He is pacing the AL in ERA (1.94), WHIP (0.91) and FanGraphs pitching WAR (6.1). He ranks second in the junior circuit in opponents' batting average (.182) and strikeout-minus-walk rate (25.0%). He has allowed one or zero runs in 21 starts. That's a Yankees franchise record and something only two other pitchers age-25 or younger have accomplished in the Live Ball Era (since 1920): Blake Snell (2018) and Dean Chance (1964). He seems like a lock for the AL Cy Young Award at this point, but Schlittler will receive his fair share of MVP love.
Schlittler hasn't been the only indispensable Yankee this year. While New York has been without Aaron Judge for a large portion of the season and has missed other star bats as well due to injuries, Rice has been a constant. He ranks third in the AL in homers (39) and runs scored (100). He's fourth in the league in RBIs (95) and OPS (.888), and tied for fourth in batting run value (+34). With two homers during the final week, Rice would become just the second non-Judge Yankee over the past decade to hit at least 41 homers in a season, joining Juan Soto (2024).
Others receiving votes: Willson Contreras, Red Sox; Pete Alonso, Orioles; Kevin McGonigle, Tigers; Miguel Vargas, White Sox; Randy Arozarena, Mariners; Munetaka Murakami, White Sox; Dylan Cease, Blue Jays
NATIONAL LEAGUE
Last month, PCA jumped over Ohtani and into the No. 1 spot in our poll. This month, he has run away from the rest of the field. The recipient of every first-place vote cast by our panel, Crow-Armstrong is tied with Kyle Schwarber for the MLB lead in home runs (45). No one has more runs (118), extra-base hits (83) or total bases (351) this season. With 38 steals, the Cubs' dynamic center fielder could become the seventh member of the 40-40 club later this week. Oh, and let's not overlook the fact that he is arguably the best defensive player at any position right now. It's no longer a question of whether Crow-Armstrong is the NL MVP. The award is as good as his right now. But will he win it in unanimous fashion?
Ohtani remains the clear runner-up in the NL despite playing in just three games this month due to his nagging left knee and right biceps injuries. The good news is Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said "there's a good chance" Ohtani will be activated from the 15-day injured list Wednesday after a minimum stint. He won't pitch for the rest of the season, leaving him with a 1.79 ERA and 95 K's over 85 2/3 innings. But Ohtani will have a few games to add to his offensive totals (30 homers, 142 wRC+).
We mentioned earlier how Schlittler looks like the heavy favorite for the AL Cy Young Award. Misiorowski is an even bigger shoo-in in the senior circuit. Through 169 1/3 innings, Miz leads the Majors in just about every category, including ERA (1.86), WHIP (0.80), strikeout-minus-walk rate (31.7%) and fWAR (6.5), to name just a few. Opposing batters have a scant .474 OPS against Misiorowski, which is the second-lowest by any qualified starter in the Divisional Era (since 1969). Pedro Martinez, in one of the greatest seasons by a pitcher, recorded a .473 opponents' OPS in 2000.
De La Cruz, who didn't receive a single vote in our previous MVP poll, has been red-hot for Cincinnati over the past month. In his last 27 games, he is batting .404 with eight homers, six steals and a 1.205 OPS. He collected multiple hits in 14 of those games, and his 2.5 fWAR during this period is the best in the big leagues. This prolonged hot streak has given De La Cruz a career-best 139 wRC+ and has left him two homers and two steals away from becoming the fourth Red in the 30-30 club and the first since Brandon Phillips in 2007.
Schwarber has fallen into a bit of a rut, going 4-for-34 with one home run over his past 10 games. He's also eight strikeouts away from setting a new record for K's in a single season. Even so, you have to admire Schwarber's consistency. He will end up with more than 40 homers and 150 games played in four of the past five seasons. He has surpassed 100 walks for a fourth consecutive season, and a third NL home run title is right there for the taking, too.
Others receiving votes: Fernando Tatis Jr., Padres; Brice Turang, Brewers; Matt Olson, Braves; James Wood, Nationals; Jordan Walker, Cardinals; Alex Bregman, Cubs; Bryce Harper, Phillies; Jake Bauers, Brewers; Otto Lopez, Marlins; Gabriel Moreno, Diamondbacks; Rafael Devers, Giants; Alec Burleson, Cardinals; CJ Abrams, Nationals; Corbin Carroll, Diamondbacks; Cristopher Sánchez, Phillies

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] MLB Injury Report: Dodgers to get Shohei Ohtani, Andy Pages, and Roki Sasaki back for postseason run
item.dc:creator: Jorge Montanez
item.description: In this week's Injury Report, the Dodgers are getting a number of key players back this week as they prepare for another deep playoff run in their quest to three-peat. Alex Bregman hopes to return sometime in the postseason after suffering multiple facial fractures in a terrible, freak accident on the on-deck circle. And Dylan Cease has likely made his last start after experiencing shoulder fatigue. That and more in the final week's injury report. ⚾️ Baseball is back! MLB returns to NBC and Peac
item.content:encoded:
In this week's Injury Report, the Dodgers are getting a number of key players back this week as they prepare for another deep playoff run in their quest to three-peat. Alex Bregman hopes to return sometime in the postseason after suffering multiple facial fractures in a terrible, freak accident on the on-deck circle. And Dylan Cease has likely made his last start after experiencing shoulder fatigue. That and more in the final week's injury report.
⚾️ Baseball is back! MLB returns to NBC and Peacock in 2026! In addition to becoming the exclusive home of Sunday Night Baseball, NBC Sports will broadcast MLB Sunday Leadoff, "Opening Day" and Labor Day primetime games, the first round of the MLB Draft, the entire Wild Card round of the postseason, and much more.
Shohei Ohtani (knee, biceps)
Andy Pages (hand)
Blake Snell (groin)
Roki Sasaki (blister)
Ohtani has been out of action for the last two weeks, sidelined with lingering knee and biceps injuries. Manager Dave Roberts told reporters on Sunday that the 32-year-old star should be expected to return from the injured list and join the Dodgers lineup on Wednesday. Ohtani should be in the lineup for the remaining games to get some needed at-bats before the postseason. The team also gets Pages back this week, activating him from the injured list ahead of Tuesday's series opener against the Padres. He's been out for a month with a left hand fracture. The two additions this week are obviously a significant boost for a Dodgers team looking to three-peat. Their returns likely shift rookie Josue De Paula to a reserve or utility role.
On the pitching side, Snell left his start last Wednesday against the Reds with left groin tightness. He stated the issue was not serious and plans on making one more start before the postseason. That start isn't going to come when his spot in the rotation comes up on Tuesday, but the plan is for him to pitch over the weekend, according to Roberts.
From Yordan Alvarez to Zack Wheeler, an A-to-Z look at the players, performances, and trends that defined the 2026 MLB regular season.
Alex Bregman (face)
Bregman was struck by a foul ball while on the on-deck circle on Sunday against the Reds and was sent to the hospital, where he was diagnosed with multiple facial fractures. The freak accident is an unfortunate development this late in the season as the Cubs prepare to enter the playoffs. The team is hoping to get their 32-year-old star third baseman back at some point in the postseason, and it is a relief that the injury didn't result in anything more serious. Meanwhile, Sasaki was activated on Monday after missing some time with a blister issue and will pitch as a one-inning reliever, auditioning for a spot in the Dodgers bullpen in the postseason.
Dylan Cease (shoulder)
Cease has likely made his final start of the season. The 30-year-old right-hander underwent an MRI on his right shoulder over the weekend after experiencing some fatigue. The imaging revealed some shoulder inflammation, but no structural damage that would require surgery, and nothing that would bring into question his availability for next season. With the Blue Jays 3.5 games out of a Wild Card spot, it doesn't make much sense for Cease to push for one more start over the final weekend. If his season is indeed over, he'll end the year with a strong 2.40 ERA, 1.10 WHIP, and 239 strikeouts over 169 innings.
Andrés Muñoz (knee)
Muñoz left Sunday's game against the Rockies with a knee injury after giving up a home run and a walk. He was set to undergo an MRI on his right knee, the results of which are still unknown. The 27-year-old right-hander had a tough, disappointing season, posting a 4.24 ERA, 1.22 WHIP, and 89 strikeouts over 57 1/3 innings while converting 28 of 38 save chances. If he's unable to pitch over the final week, it could be Seranthony Domíguez closing out the remaining games.
Bryce Eldridge (concussion)
More Giants injuries that seemingly come out of nowhere. Eldridge was scratched from Friday's lineup against the Dodgers due to a head laceration after bumping his head on a low-hanging ceiling at the team hotel. He still "felt woozy" throughout the weekend and entered the concussion protocol before the team ultimately placed him on the 7-day concussion injured list. The move is retroactive to Friday, so there's a chance he could return for the final weekend series, though that's probably unlikely. The 21-year-old slugger flashed immense potential this season, hitting .269/.364/.461 with 17 homers and 57 RBI across 448 plate appearances.
Colt Keith (thumb)
Keith's season is over after the team placed him on the 10-day injured list with a left thumb sprain. It's an issue that the 25-year-old infielder has been playing through over the last several weeks. He ends the season hitting a modest .258/.322/.406 with 10 homers, 51 runs scored, 36 RBI, and six steals across 423 plate appearances.

item.title: [New York Post] Dodgers’ plan for Shohei Ohtani is unnecessarily risky
item.dc:creator: Dylan Hernandez
item.description: The Dodgers have lost this gamble once before. But that won’t stop them from placing the same wager again. Rather than take every precaution to ensure Shohei Ohtani doesn’t worsen the injuries to his right arm and left knee, the Dodgers will prioritize giving him at-bats to get him ready for the playoffs. Ohtani is expected to be activated from the 15-day injured list Wednesday, and manager Dave Roberts said the plan is for him to play in every one of the five games that remain in the regular se
item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers have lost this gamble once before. But that won’t stop them from placing the same wager again.
Rather than take every precaution to ensure Shohei Ohtani doesn’t worsen the injuries to his right arm and left knee, the Dodgers will prioritize giving him at-bats to get him ready for the playoffs.
Ohtani is expected to be activated from the 15-day injured list Wednesday, and manager Dave Roberts said the plan is for him to play in every one of the five games that remain in the regular season.
“He’ll need those live at-bats,” Roberts said.
This feels reckless — and unnecessarily risky, especially when considering what happened the last time the Dodgers were in this position, just earlier this month.
Ohtani was experiencing discomfort in his arm and knee. The Dodgers downplayed the severity of his injuries, with general manager Brandon Gomes claiming the physical problems weren’t responsible for his hitting slump and shouldn’t require him to be placed on the IL.
So much for that.
Roberts described Ohtani as being “pain-free” Sunday, but acknowledged he was still experiencing “discomfort you can play through.” Certain levels of discomfort can be tolerated — until they can’t be, of course. That’s been the story of Ohtani’s season.
When Ohtani started feeling pain in his knee, he insisted he could pitch through it. Until he couldn’t.
When he started to be affected in the batter’s box by the throbbing in his arm and knee, he claimed he could play it. Until he couldn’t.
Roberts said Ohtani’s condition has improved over the last two weeks. But Roberts also didn’t claim Ohtani was completely healthy.
“Is he 100%?” Roberts said. “Probably not.”
In other words, what bothered Ohtani when he landed on the IL still bothers him, just not as much.
This is a problem.
What happened earlier this month showed that if Ohtani plays too many games with these particular injuries, he will reach a point where he won’t even be able to take the field.
Why not give Ohtani every other game off? Will playing five more regular-season games instead of three make that much of a difference? Because the question isn’t whether Ohtani can make it through the next five games. The question is how much closer these games will push him to the point of no return.
The objective should be to make sure Ohtani is available in some capacity throughout the entire postseason, not only at the start of it. If he has to be gradually work his way into form over the playoffs, so be it.
Ohtani would almost certainly reject such cautious thinking. He doesn’t like half-measures. Ohtani takes big swings without much regard to the consequences.
So, if he’s going to use the final week of the regular season to prepare for the playoffs, he’ll probably do so with visions of being an impact player. He doesn’t want a Kirk Gibson moment; he wants to be Mr. October.
Before he went on the IL, Ohtani offered a realistic assessment of his health, saying he didn’t expect to be at 100% between now and the end of the season. But he said he believed he could overcome his physical problems by making adjustments to his swing.
“With some creativity, I think I can make up for what’s not right,” Ohtani said in Japanese. “Another way to say it is that it’s an opportunity to create new ways to compete.”
At the time, that meant learning how to hit with one arm and one leg.
The Dodgers let him, and Ohtani ended up on the IL.
Once again, it sounds as if Ohtani is determined to squeeze in as many at-bats as possible, and once again, it sounds as if the Dodgers will let him try.
This approach has significant upside — and downside, too.

item.title: [marca usa] Dave Roberts sobre Shohei Ohtani: “Hay una buena posibilidad de que lo veamos en la próxima serie”
item.dc:creator: Jose Escobar
item.description: - MLB. Wyatt Langford salta sobre el catcher de Toronto en una espectacular jugada de los Rangers - MLB. Aaron Judge desata la preocupación tras abandonar el juego por una lesión repentina días después de volver a MLB Existe cierta preocupación entre los aficionados sobre cuánto tiempo necesitará Shohei Ohtani para recuperarse antes de volver finalmente con los Los Angeles Dodgers, quienes ya aseguraron su boleto a los playoffs y buscan disputar su tercera Serie Mundial consecutiva. Afortunadame
item.content:encoded:
- MLB. Wyatt Langford salta sobre el catcher de Toronto en una espectacular jugada de los Rangers
- MLB. Aaron Judge desata la preocupación tras abandonar el juego por una lesión repentina días después de volver a MLB
Existe cierta preocupación entre los aficionados sobre cuánto tiempo necesitará Shohei Ohtani para recuperarse antes de volver finalmente con los Los Angeles Dodgers, quienes ya aseguraron su boleto a los playoffs y buscan disputar su tercera Serie Mundial consecutiva.
Afortunadamente para los Dodgers, el regreso de la estrella japonesa está cada vez más cerca después de dar otro paso positivo en su recuperación ofensiva, por lo que podría volver tan pronto como el inicio de la próxima serie ante los San Diego Padres.
¿Qué dijo Dave Roberts sobre Shohei Ohtani?
El manager Dave Roberts confirmó que Ohtani (molestias en el bíceps derecho y la rodilla izquierda) continúa con una evolución favorable y está cada vez más cerca de regresar a la acción. El japonés podría ser activado de la lista de lesionados de 15 días durante la próxima serie de Los Ángeles.
“Hay una buena posibilidad de que lo veamos en la próxima serie”, aseguró Roberts después de la victoria de los Dodgers por 10-4 sobre los Giants en el Dodger Stadium.
Ohtani fue colocado en la lista de lesionados con fecha retroactiva al 8 de septiembre, por lo que sería elegible para regresar el miércoles, en el segundo partido de la última serie de temporada regular como local ante los San Diego Padres. Su regreso será únicamente como bateador, ya que los Dodgers decidieron detener por ahora su actividad como lanzador.
El astro japonés ya comenzó a recuperar ritmo en la caja de bateo. Después de iniciar su programa de progresión ofensiva el martes, Ohtani dio el siguiente paso al enfrentar lanzamientos de la máquina Trajekt, un dispositivo que simula enfrentar a pitchers reales.
De acuerdo con Roberts, el japonés terminó con buenas sensaciones después de realizar entre 30 y 40 swings el sábado, además de trabajar en el corrido de bases durante la práctica de bateo.
Una recuperación fugaz antes de los playoffs
Si Ohtani regresa el miércoles, cuando sea elegible para salir de la lista de lesionados, solamente tendrá cinco partidos de temporada regular para recuperar ritmo, encontrar nuevamente su timing en el plato y adaptarse a la intensidad de las Grandes Ligas antes del inicio de la postemporada.
Por ello, Dave Roberts planea colocarlo en la alineación en todos los encuentros disponibles, ya que el japonés necesita acumular turnos reales al bate para recuperar confianza y llegar en mejores condiciones al momento más importante del año.
Ohtani tampoco tendrá una asignación de rehabilitación en Ligas Menores, debido a que la temporada regular de Triple-A termina el domingo y los Dodgers no cuentan con pitchers adicionales disponibles para realizar sesiones de bateo en vivo.

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

22 Sep 2026, 03:25 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Denis Poroy)
The hottest team in baseball is racing toward a playoff berth, and the San Diego Padres can complete the chase as early as Tuesday's opener of a three-game road series against the Los Angeles Dodgers.
The Padres (87-69) have won 13 of their last 14 games to not only climb out of wild-card uncertainty but also give themselves a legitimate chance at clinching the National League's top wild-card spot over their final six regular-season games.
They can clinch a playoff spot Tuesday with a win and an Arizona Diamondbacks loss to the Colorado Rockies.
A postseason appearance would be the third consecutive for San Diego, which has never delivered a similar run in franchise history.
'This is so fun,' said Jake Cronenworth, who had two home runs and five RBIs for San Diego in its 7-3 home victory over the Miami Marlins on Sunday. 'It's hard to compare each (of the past three playoff chases). Each one's so fun in its own way and unique. But this one's been really awesome.'
Fernando Tatis Jr. added a home run, his 25th, and is batting .310 with 12 home runs and a 1.016 OPS over his past 30 games since Aug. 18.
Against their Southern California rival, the Padres are expected to send right-hander Michael King (12-9, 3.03 ERA) to the mound.
King is 4-0 with a 1.41 ERA over his last five starts and is 1-1 with a 3.12 ERA in three starts against the Dodgers this season, including an outing in May when he went seven scoreless innings. That start included a season-high nine strikeouts.
The Dodgers (96-60) also have plenty to play for after clinching the National League West title last week. They are two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers for the best record in the NL but do not hold the tiebreaker between the teams.
Los Angeles is 14-3 since Sept. 3 and has a magic number of three to clinch a top-two spot in the NL and a bye into the NL Division Series.While the Padres are on a five-game winning streak, the Dodgers have won four in a row after completing a three-game home sweep of the San Francisco Giants.
Tommy Edman hit a game-tying home run in the sixth inning for Los Angeles on Sunday, while Enrique Hernandez had a go-ahead RBI double in the seventh.
While right-hander Roki Sasaki (5-5, 4.60) is set to return from a blister issue, he will have an abbreviated outing and not necessarily as the starter. Manager Dave Roberts characterized the pitching plan as more of a bullpen game.
The Dodgers are also expected to see the return of center fielder Andy Pages for the series opener against the Padres. Pages has not played since Aug. 21 because of a broken hand.
While the Dodgers have found some success over the past three-plus weeks following a lackluster two months, their 14-3 run has not come against teams who are in playoff contention. A visit from the Padres changes that.
'I think it's going to be a good kind of primer,' Roberts said. 'They're a very talented team. They're playing as good as anyone in all of baseball. I'm looking forward to playing those guys and just kind of ramping it up a little bit more for our guys.'
--Field Level Media

item.title: [FanSided] Dave Roberts' handling of Roki Sasaki shows why the Dodgers keep winning
item.dc:creator: Jake Elman
item.description: If you needed yet another reminder of why Dave Roberts has led the Los Angeles Dodgers to three championships in six years, look no further than his treatment of Roki Sasaki. Roberts has both built Sasaki up and held the Japanese import accountable through two up-and-down seasons. He hasn’t been stubbornly loyal to the 24-year-old righty, nor has he waved the white flag amid Sasaki’s continued control issues. item.content:encoded:
If you needed yet another reminder of why Dave Roberts has led the Los Angeles Dodgers to three championships in six years, look no further than his treatment of Roki Sasaki.
Roberts has both built Sasaki up and held the Japanese import accountable through two up-and-down seasons. He hasn’t been stubbornly loyal to the 24-year-old righty, nor has he waved the white flag amid Sasaki’s continued control issues.
As Sasaki nears a return from the IL, Roberts confirmed that Sasaki will start pitching out of the bullpen this week. All signs point to Sasaki serving as a reliever for the second straight postseason.
Sasaki has missed nearly all of September with a hip injury, and he should have some extra time to recover. The Dodgers are closing in one of the NL’s top two playoff seeds, which includes a first-round bye.
Does Roki Sasaki deserve to make the Los Angeles Dodgers’ playoff roster?
Before looking ahead to October, let’s quickly travel back to this past spring. I repeatedly questioned Sasaki’s viability as an MLB starter, largely because of his control and what felt like an inability to handle the pressure associated with pitching Stateside.
Honestly? I really haven’t changed my opinion, though I’ll give Sasaki his flowers. He’s played some of his best baseball in the second half, recording a 3.05 ERA in seven starts. That’s down from 5.33 over 15 first-half outings, though he’s still struggling to make it through five innings.
Most importantly, he’s significantly cut down on his homers, allowing three in 38.1 innings. That’s a fantastic improvement from the 19 long balls he gave up in 81 first-half innings.
So what’s the problem? Walks. I’m old school, so I don’t like young pitchers only working five innings because they can’t hit the strike zone. Sasaki has issued 15 free passes in those 38.1 innings, and it drives up his pitch count.
At the end of the day, Sasaki has completed six innings in just seven of his 22 starts. Now is the perfect time to permanently transition him to a relief role.
But we asked whether Sasaki deserves to be on the playoff roster, and despite my criticism, the answer is an easy “yes.” There’s something to be said about a young player admitting to confidence issues yet powering through and trying to make things work rather than let things spiral.
What’s especially admirable about Sasaki is that he doesn’t complain or make himself out to be a victim. He’s never targeted the media, which has actually had his back for much of the last two years. He’s certainly not teammate Kyle Tucker, whose body language and work ethic have raised red flags dating back to his brief stint with the Cubs.
Maybe Sasaki is the Dodgers’ secret playoff weapon once again. We’d certainly feel more comfortable trusting him in October instead of embattled former closer Edwin Díaz.
Yikes. Imagine reading that on Opening Day.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers Get Tyler Glasnow Injury Update After Last Week's Ominous Report
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Sandoval; Unknown
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers star pitcher Tyler Glasnow shut down any injury concerns on Friday after a scare last week. Glasnow looked like his usual self against the San Francisco Giants. He allowed only two runs on three hits and two walks while striking out 10 over six innings to earn his fifth win of the season. item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers star pitcher Tyler Glasnow shut down any injury concerns on Friday after a scare last week.
Glasnow looked like his usual self against the San Francisco Giants. He allowed only two runs on three hits and two walks while striking out 10 over six innings to earn his fifth win of the season.
Dodgers skipper Dave Roberts couldn't be more pleased with his outing and, more importantly, loves to see Glasnow healthy heading into the postseason.
“It is just making sure he’s feeling good, he’s healthy, which he is,” Roberts said. “So now it’s just letting him go do what he does and bet on the talent to perform. That’s where I think we all feel good, especially Tyler right now, just knowing the health and where the head’s at, all that stuff. We’re in a good spot.”
Roberts' tone on Friday was different than Glasnow's last outing on Sunday against Miami.
“He’s a big-bodied guy, so there’s a lot of big moving parts,” Roberts said last Sunday. “So sometimes if they get out of whack a little bit, it’s hard to just sync everything up.”
Last week, Glasnow's outing was concerning. Not only did he get the loss against the Miami Marlins, but the 33-year-old was also far from himself.
Roberts said he "didn't feel great" after the fact.
Nonetheless, Glasnow noted that there was nothing to be worried about.
“It wasn’t anything crazy,” Glasnow said. “But I definitely feel better now than I did then."
“Right now, I feel pretty good,” he added. “We worked on some stuff after that last start. Just tried to keep for this start, take it in the next start. And then hopefully everything is feeling good for playoffs.”
Tyler Glasnow Looking to Round Into Form Before Postseason
Glasnow's outing on Friday was his fifth since returning from the 60-day IL.
The 33-year-old dealt with a back injury that held him to seven starts. Before his return in late August, Glasnow last pitched in early May.
Overall, Glasnow has tallied a 3.46 ERA, 87 strikeouts and a 0.96 WHIP in 67.2 innings this season. He'll be relied upon heavily come October as the team's fourth starter.
Glasnow is in his third season in Los Angeles after the Dodgers traded for him in December 2023. In that time, Glasnow has landed on the injured list multiple times but has been stellar when healthy.
In 52 games, Glasnow has a 18-10 record, 361 strikeouts, a 3.39 ERA and a 0.99 WHIP in 292 innings.
He made six appearances (three starts) in last year's postseason, sporting a 1.69 ERA across 21.1 innings with 25 strikeouts. He earned the save in Game 6 of the World Series and took down seven outs in Game 7.

Ricardo Sandoval is a freelance writer with On SI. He is a graduate of California State University, Northridge, and specializes in sports writing, particularly in MLB, NBA and NFL. He previously served as an Associate Editor for Dodgers Nation and has worked with Newsweek and The Sporting News.

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Dave Roberts Hints at Possible October Change at Top of Lineup
item.dc:creator: Steve Webb
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CA — The Dodgers still expect Shohei Ohtani back in the lineup before October, and Dave Roberts made clear Saturday that his first instinct remains to put Ohtani right back atop the batting order. But the manager is also preparing for the possibility that things don’t go exactly according to plan. With Ohtani still sidelined and his return date uncertain, Mookie Betts has moved back into the leadoff spot, a familiar home for the former MVP. After Friday night’s two-homer performance
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CA — The Dodgers still expect Shohei Ohtani back in the lineup before October, and Dave Roberts made clear Saturday that his first instinct remains to put Ohtani right back atop the batting order.
But the manager is also preparing for the possibility that things don’t go exactly according to plan.
With Ohtani still sidelined and his return date uncertain, Mookie Betts has moved back into the leadoff spot, a familiar home for the former MVP. After Friday night’s two-homer performance against the Giants, Roberts acknowledged that Betts could become an alternative at the top of the order if the Dodgers need to make an adjustment in October.
“Certainly there is uncertainty with Sho, all the while expecting him to be back,” Roberts said. “But you do got to kind of prepare for whatever. I just think that Mookie is swinging the bat. He’s hit there many times throughout his career. So it just kind of makes sense.”
Betts certainly looked comfortable there Friday. He reached base four times, homered twice and drove in three runs as the Dodgers beat San Francisco 8-2. Long before Ohtani arrived in Los Angeles, Betts was one of baseball’s premier leadoff hitters, so moving him back there isn’t exactly unfamiliar territory.
Roberts has also been encouraged by the quality of Betts’ at-bats during his recent surge.
“I think with Mookie, results drive kind of his demeanor,” Roberts said. “With the results, I think that he is considerably better. He’s not a chase guy anyway, but he’s cut that down considerably. The quality of contact is considerably higher, and then now you’ve got that attitude, that confidence that we’re used to seeing with Mookie.”
For now, Roberts still expects Ohtani to reclaim the leadoff spot once he returns.
“That’s my first kind of thought,” Roberts said. “But until he gets back, or when he gets back, then I’ll kind of potentially redirect, react if it’s a left-right situation, or just supplant him back there in the one.”
That leaves the Dodgers with some flexibility. If Ohtani immediately looks like himself, there may be nothing to discuss. But if he needs time to regain his timing after the layoff, the Dodgers don’t have to force the issue at the top of the lineup. Betts has spent most of his career proving he can handle that job.
The Dodgers are also continuing to work Will Smith back toward a normal workload after his own stint on the injured list. Smith was in the lineup Saturday for a second consecutive game, only the third time he has caught back-to-back games since returning.
“I think he’s come along well,” Roberts said. “I think his swing is in a much better spot, getting better, consistent.”
The Dodgers intentionally scheduled Smith for consecutive games this weekend before giving him two days to recover with Monday’s off day included. Roberts said Smith would then play two or three games in the following series.
“I think it’s a good exercise for him,” Roberts said.
Smith’s return matters well beyond his bat. Roberts also pointed to the growing comfort between Smith and Tarik Skubal after their latest game together, saying the pitcher and catcher finally appeared to reach a point of “mutual trust” regarding the game plan and how Skubal wanted to attack hitters.
That relationship will matter considerably if Skubal is asked to pitch deep into October.
The larger picture is that the Dodgers are beginning to have options again. Smith is rebuilding his workload. Betts is swinging the bat with confidence. Ohtani is expected back. And if Ohtani isn’t immediately ready to carry the leadoff responsibilities, the Dodgers have one of the most accomplished leadoff hitters of his generation waiting right behind him.
There are worse backup plans to have in October.
More Dodgers Coverage:
Have you subscribed to the Bleed Los Podcast YouTube channel? Be sure to ring the notification bell to watch player interviews, participate in shows & promotions, and stay up to date on all Dodgers news and rumors!
A lifelong baseball fan, Webb has been going to Dodger games since he moved to Los Angeles in 1987. His favorite memory was attending the insane Game 3 of the World Series in 2025 and hugging random Dodgers fans after Freddie’s walkoff homer. He has been writing for Dodgersbeat since 2020.

item.title: [USA Today] Window tightens for Shohei Ohtani to get ready for playoffs
item.dc:creator: Josh Peter
item.description: Window tightens for Shohei Ohtani to get ready for playoffs Shohei Ohtani’s swing is among the most dangerous in baseball. The Los Angeles Dodgers will have only five games to get it ready for the playoffs, barring any setbacks. There have been many of them for Ohtani, who’s missed the past 12 games while dealing with issues to his left knee and right biceps. He’s expected to be back in the Dodgers' lineup in the team's upcoming series against the San Diego Padres. There will be only five games
item.content:encoded:
Window tightens for Shohei Ohtani to get ready for playoffs
Shohei Ohtani’s swing is among the most dangerous in baseball. The Los Angeles Dodgers will have only five games to get it ready for the playoffs, barring any setbacks.
There have been many of them for Ohtani, who’s missed the past 12 games while dealing with issues to his left knee and right biceps. He’s expected to be back in the Dodgers' lineup in the team's upcoming series against the San Diego Padres. There will be only five games left in the regular season.
Because of Ohtani’s lingering knee issues, the Dodgers have shut him down from pitching. But they’d still like him to bat – and a swing that has generated a team-leading 30 home runs this season and 263 over the last six seasons.
In his last 24 games before going on the injured reserve list, however, Ohtani hit .198 (19-for-96) with 34 strikeouts.
It raises a premature, although not outrageous, question involving the four-time MVP: At some point, in some cases, might the Dodgers be better off with Ohtani out of the lineup?
Precious at-bats
The Dodgers haven’t had enough pitchers to throw him live batting practice, and so he’s been hitting off the Trajekt, a machine that simulates real pitchers. And so those final five regular-season games – two against the Padres and three against the San Francisco Giants – because even more critical.
"I do think that when he's activated, it's going to be the best physical place he's been in in quite some time,’’ said Dodgers manager Dave Roberts, per Sonja Chen of MLB.com.
So we’ll see if feeling good translates into swinging well for Ohtani.
The Dodgers have managed to win despite missing their MVP designated hitter. Ohtani’s missed 15 of the Dodgers’ last 16 games, and the team has gone 13-3 without him. In six of those games, the Dodgers won by two or fewer runs.
The Dodgers, who clinched a playoff berth by winning the NL West crown, have a four-game lead on the Atlanta Braves to clinch a first-round bye. Los Angeles is two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers for the No. 1 season and homefield advantage through the NL playoffs.
At-bats figure to become even more precious as the playoffs begin.
Ohtani might have to earn them.

item.content:encoded:
- Los Angeles Dodgers. Roster Move: Skubal to Bereavement List, Sheehan recalled by Dodgers
- Los Angeles Dodgers. Ohtani ramps up hitting progression: Why Dave Roberts is bullish on star's October return
There is some concern among fans about how much time Shohei Ohtani will need to recover before finally returning to the Los Angeles Dodgers, who have already clinched a playoff spot and are looking to reach their third consecutive World Series.
Fortunately for the Dodgers, the Japanese superstar’s return is getting closer after taking another positive step in his offensive recovery, meaning he could be back as soon as the start of the next series against the San Diego Padres.
What did Dave Roberts say about Shohei Ohtani?
Manager Dave Roberts confirmed that Ohtani (right biceps and left knee issues) continues to make positive progress and is getting closer to returning to action. The Japanese star could be activated from the 15-day injured list during the Dodgers’ upcoming series.
There's a good chance next series we'll see him
Roberts said after Los Angeles’ 10-4 win over the Giants at Dodger Stadium.
Ohtani was placed on the injured list retroactive to September 8, making him eligible to return Wednesday, in the second game of the Dodgers’ final regular-season home series against the San Diego Padres. His return will only be as a hitter, as the Dodgers have paused his pitching activities for now.
The Japanese star has already begun regaining his timing at the plate. After starting his offensive progression program on Tuesday, Ohtani took the next step by facing pitches from the Trajekt machine, a device that simulates facing real pitchers. According to Roberts, Ohtani felt good after taking 30 to 40 swings on Saturday and also worked on running the bases during batting practice.
A quick recovery before the playoffs
If Ohtani returns on Wednesday, when he becomes eligible to come off the injured list, he will have only five regular-season games to regain his rhythm, find his timing again, and readjust to the intensity of Major League Baseball before the postseason begins.
For that reason, Dave Roberts plans to put him in the lineup for every available game, as the Japanese star needs to accumulate live at-bats to rebuild confidence and be in better shape for the most important part of the year.
Ohtani will also not have a Minor League rehab assignment, as the Triple-A regular season ends Sunday and the Dodgers do not have additional pitchers available to conduct live batting practice sessions.

item.content:encoded:
¡Regreso estelar! Dodgers recupera a Shohei Ohtani para su última serie ante Padres
Ohtani estaría de regreso en la alineación de los Dodgers con cinco juegos antes de iniciar los playoffs.
La estancia de Shohei Ohtani en la lista de lesionados de las Grandes Ligas de Béisbol (MLB) podría durar el mínimo posible, ya que, de acuerdo con el manager Dave Roberts, el estelar pelotero japonés de los Dodgers estaría de regreso en la alineación para el juego de este miércoles 23 de septiembre ante los Padres.
Ohtani fue colocado en la lista de lesionados por 15 días con fecha retroactiva al 8 de septiembre debido a las constantes molestias en la rodilla izquierda y su bíceps derecho. Después de otro productivo día bateando, Ohtani sigue en camino para volver como el bateador designado de los Dodgers durante su última serie de la temporada regular en casa.
“Es muy probable que lo veamos en la próxima serie”, dijo Roberts.
El pasado martes 15 de septiembre, Ohtani retomó sus actividades de bateo y el sábado finalmente comenzó a batear con la máquina Trajekt, la cual simula el movimiento de los pitcheos de lanzadores reales. Ohtani se habría sentido bien luego de hacer entre 30 y 40 swings, además de correr las bases.
Ohtani conectó 30 jonrones, cifra máxima para los Dodgers en la temporada, antes de quedar fuera de acción debido a las constantes molestias físicas. En 24 juegos antes de aterrizar en la lista de lesionados, mismo lapso en el que retomó su programa para lanzar, Shohei cayó estrepitosamente bateando .198 (de 96-19) con 34 ponches.
Si todo sale conforme al plan, los Dodgers tendrán a Ohtani para los últimos cinco juegos de la temporada regular, todos ellos de suma importancia antes de comenzar los playoffs. Por ello, el manager Dave Roberts tiene planeado alinearlo en todos los juegos posibles para que Ohtani tome turnos al bate, especialmente porque no tendrá una asignación de rehabilitación en las Ligas Menores.
Aún con su ausencia en 15 de los últimos 16 juegos, los Dodgers se las han arreglado para firmar un gran cierre firmando una marca de 13-3 en sus 16 juegos más recientes.
Si bien los Dodgers saben que Ohtani no volverá al cien por ciento físicamente, el equipo confía que el descanso de algunos días le permita sentirse mejor para iniciar la postemporada. El piloto aseguró que Shohei está libre de dolor, aunque eso no necesariamente significa que se haya aliviado de todas sus molestias.
“Realmente creo que, cuando sea activado estará en su mejor condición física en bastante tiempo”, sentenció Roberts.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers playoff roster projection: Could Edwin Díaz, Josue De Paula, even Hyeseong Kim surprise?

item.content:encoded:
Entering the final week of the regular season, the Dodgers more or less know their postseason fate.
They've locked up the National League West. They are a seemingly safe four games clear of the Atlanta Braves for a first-round bye. And, unless they can close a two-game gap on the Milwaukee Brewers without holding the tiebreaker, they will finish as the NL's No. 2 seed, getting home-field advantage at least for the NL Division Series.
Thus, the real intrigue for now is who might be on the Dodgers' postseason roster when the playoffs begin next month.
This year, injuries and fluctuating performances have forced them to cycle 53 different players through their clubhouse.
And while the core of the group is clear, many questions remain about how the club will construct its lineup and pitching staff for this fall's pursuit of a third-straight World Series.
Here is the California Post's best guess about how it will all shake out.
Lineup locks
Will Smith, Freddie Freeman, Tommy Edman, Mookie Betts, Max Muncy, Teoscar Hernández, Andy Pages, Kyle Tucker, Shohei Ohtani, Kiké Hernández, Miguel Rojas, Hunter Feduccia
There won't be any big surprises in how the Dodgers line up to begin the playoffs, assuming Ohtani is healthy enough to resume everyday DH'ing duties.
Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker have cemented their place as everyday hitters thanks to late-season surges. Andy Pages is due back on Tuesday from a fractured hand. Freddie Freeman still seems somewhat limited by his right knee injury, but has nonetheless been able to manage it well enough to this point. And while Tommy Edman has been slumping lately, he doesn't seem to be in immediate danger of losing at-bats.
On the bench, Hunter Feduccia has locked up the back-up catching job, and could be a left-handed hitting option as a pinch-hitter. Kiké Hernández and Miguel Rojas, meanwhile, each provide versatile defensive depth, as well as extensive track records for postseason heroics when called upon.
Entering the final week of the regular season, the core of the Dodgers' position player group looks as they expected.
Dodgers Lineup questions
Bubble candidates: Josue De Paula, Dalton Rushing, Alex Call, Alex Freeland, Hyeseong Kim
The Dodgers will still have one, if not two, position player spots to fill depending on how they construct their roster (i.e. an even 13 pitchers/13 hitters, or a 12/14 split like they used last year?)
And for those, they could have a number of difficult decisions.
First and foremost: Will Josue De Paula make the playoff roster?
If he does, it will likely be as a left-handed bench bat; though if there is any lingering uncertainty with Ohtani, he could also provide insurance as a backup DH option. His main competition right now figures to be Alex Call (who might be redundant to Rojas and Hernández as a right-handed bench bat) or Dalton Rushing (who is an intriguing alternative as a left-handed bat, but remains sidelined from the setback he suffered with his elbow injury earlier this month).
In just 10 MLB games, De Paula has quickly built a strong case, showing supreme plate discipline (10 walks to only four strikeouts) and the potential for power (three doubles, one home run, seven RBIs). At this point, it might be more of a surprise if he doesn't make it.
If the Dodgers elect to carry an extra position player on top of that, the choices are even more varied.
Last year, they rostered two base-running/defensive specialists throughout the playoffs in infielder Hyeseong Kim and outfielder Justin Dean. Dean is now gone, and Hernández could serve as a late-game defensive outfield replacement anyway. But Kim remains in consideration, manager Dave Roberts said, thanks to his speed and infield glove. Alex Freeland could also factor in here, as someone capable of providing more at the plate.
Lineup projection for Los Angeles
C: Will Smith
1B: Freddie Freeman
2B: Tommy Edman
SS: Mookie Betts
3B: Max Muncy
LF: Teoscar Hernández
CF: Andy Pages
RF: Kyle Tucker
DH: Shohei Ohtani
Bench: Kiké Hernández, Miguel Rojas, Hunter Feduccia, Josue De Paula, Hyeseong Kim*
*If the Dodgers carry 14 position players
Dodgers pitching staff locks
Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow, Roki Sasaki, Tanner Scott, Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips
The Dodgers' starting rotation is set, assuming no further setbacks with Blake Snell's groin injury. The back end of the bullpen has come into focus, too, with Tanner Scott and/or Roki Sasaki the most logical candidates to serve as closer, and Alex Vesia and Evan Phillips separating themselves as the team's next most-trusted high-leverage relief options.
The only real question here is how the Dodgers will line up the rotation. Yamamoto-Skubal would make sense for Games 1 and 2 of a division series (keeping them both on-line for a potential Game 5). But could Tyler Glasnow's potential issues with traveling tempt the Dodgers to use him primarily at home, if they can? All factors to consider in the coming weeks.
Pitching staff questions
Roster bubble candidates: Brock Stewart, Edwin Díaz, Blake Treinen, Kris Bubic, Jack Dreyer, Emmet Sheehan, Justin Wrobleski, Edgardo Henriquez, Will Klein, Eric Lauer
The first thing the Dodgers need to figure out here is health.
Edgardo Henriquez will almost certainly be on the playoff roster, and pitching in a high-leverage role, if he can make a full recovery from his recent back strain. Will Klein and Eric Lauer might also be available health-wise, though lack clear roles to step immediately back into.
Otherwise, the Dodgers will effectively have at least four open spots for six to seven other pitchers.
For added right-handed depth, they might be deciding between Brock Stewart (who has been a go-to weapon against right-handed hitters recently), Edwin Díaz (who is trying to salvage his dismal debut season, and did throw a pair of scoreless outings this weekend) and Blake Treinen (who has curiously pitched only five times in three weeks since being activated from the injured list, and not in the highest of leverage).
For another left-handed option, they could go with Kris Bubic (the trade deadline acquisition who has impressed with three scoreless appearances since returning from an injury) or Jack Dreyer (who was one of the Dodgers' best relievers from June to August, but has given up five runs in his last seven outings).
And for a multi-inning role, they will have Emmet Sheehan (who has looked like a different pitcher in three sterling starts since returning from a minor-league demotion) and Justin Wrobleski (the breakout All-Star who has finally shaken some of his home run problems since moving to the bullpen).
There are many permutations that the Dodgers could employ depending on opponent. They're still figuring out the exact hierarchy of all their bullpen arms, too.
But as long as their rotation is dominant, everything else should take care of itself.
Pitching staff projection
Rotation: Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow
Bullpen: Roki Sasaki, Tanner Scott, Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips, Brock Stewart, Kris Bubic, Edwin Díaz, Emmet Sheehan, Justin Wrobleski

item.title: [Dodger Blue] Dodgers manager Dave Roberts reveals new role for Roki Sasaki
item.dc:creator: Matt Borelli

item.content:encoded:
Roki Sasaki is among the players expected to rejoin the Los Angeles Dodgers this week as they inch closer to full strength ahead of the postseason.
The right-hander has been on the 15-day injured list since Aug. 27 due to a blister on his right middle finger, but made steady progress throughout his recovery. He has thrown multiple bullpen sessions and live batting practices this month, including 48 pitches over four innings last Wednesday.
Sasaki was originally slated to return as a starting pitcher, but he now appears headed to the bullpen for the remainder of the 2026 season. The 24-year-old is capable of pitching multiple innings as a reliever, but not in the traditional sense of a bulk pitcher.
“I can see multiples, but it’s not going to be bulk as in four or five innings. It won’t be that,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of Sasaki’s role.
Sasaki won’t be limited to simply providing length out of the bullpen. Roberts also indicated that he would feel comfortable using him in high-leverage situations, but only at the start of a “clean inning.”
As for whether Sasaki could get save opportunities, it’s something that Roberts might consider down the road.
“It won’t be in the ninth the first time, but it potentially could fall out (that way),” the Dodgers skipper said.
Tanner Scott has been the Dodgers’ primary closer in recent weeks, but Edwin Díaz recently returned from the 15-day IL and is hoping to eventually reclaim the role. Edgardo Henriquez also received save opportunities prior to landing on the IL with lower back discomfort.
Roki Sasaki’s postseason success
Sasaki shined as a reliever during the Dodgers’ World Series run last year, pitching to a minuscule 0.84 ERA and 1.03 WHIP with three saves in nine appearances. His previous success on baseball’s biggest stage played a role in the team’s decision to once again move him to the bullpen.
“Yeah. He’s done it, he’s really good, he’s a neutral pitcher, high-octane stuff,” Roberts said. “You really just need four starters, so we’re in a good spot there for now.”
Along with Sasaki, the Dodgers’ postseason bullpen could include other traditional starters such as Justin Wrobleski and Emmet Sheehan. The club’s starting rotation will feature two of the league’s best arms in Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tarik Skubal.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers have lineup problem they cannot afford to solve by benching Josue De Paula
item.dc:creator: Miracle Dimwesh
item.description: Josue De Paula was supposed to give the Los Angeles Dodgers another young bat for the final weeks of the regular season. Instead, the rookie has created a lineup problem the team may not be able to ignore. De Paula has been too productive to simply remove from the lineup. The 21-year-old has reached base at a .474 clip through his first 10 MLB games, giving the Dodgers another dangerous left-handed hitter before the postseason. That creates an interesting problem when Shohei Ohtani returns. The
item.content:encoded:
Josue De Paula was supposed to give the Los Angeles Dodgers another young bat for the final weeks of the regular season. Instead, the rookie has created a lineup problem the team may not be able to ignore.
De Paula has been too productive to simply remove from the lineup. The 21-year-old has reached base at a .474 clip through his first 10 MLB games, giving the Dodgers another dangerous left-handed hitter before the postseason.
That creates an interesting problem when Shohei Ohtani returns. The Dodgers have several established outfielders, but De Paula's bat is making it harder to find room for everyone.
Josue De Paula has been doing this all year
The rookie's hot start is not coming out of nowhere. De Paula dominated Double-A pitching throughout the season before earning his September call-up.
Minor League Baseball named him the 2026 Texas League MVP on Monday. He hit .303/.401/.547 with 27 home runs, 31 stolen bases, 152 hits and 104 RBIs in 124 games for Tulsa.
That production earned him a direct jump from Double-A to Los Angeles. He has continued showing the same offensive approach against MLB pitching.
De Paula has gone 8-for-28 with 10 walks, one home run and seven RBIs in his first 10 games. He has also played two games in left field, showing the Dodgers can move him around when necessary.
Dodgers face a difficult Ohtani lineup decision
Feb 24, 2026; Phoenix, Arizona, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Josue De Paula against the Cleveland Guardians during a spring training game at Camelback Ranch-Glendale. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
The situation becomes more complicated with Ohtani nearing a return. Manager Dave Roberts said there is a good chance Ohtani will be activated Wednesday against the San Diego Padres. He will return as a hitter, not a pitcher.
That puts Ohtani back at DH and removes the easiest path to keeping De Paula in the lineup.
The Dodgers already have Kyle Tucker in right field, Teoscar Hernández in left and Andy Pages in center. Tucker signed a four-year, $240 million deal before the season, while Hernández and Pages have remained important parts of the club's outfield plans.
De Paula can play the outfield, but moving him there would force another decision. Taking one of the established outfielders out also means changing a group that has helped Los Angeles reach this point.
The Dodgers do not have to solve the entire problem today. But De Paula's performance has made one thing clear: when Ohtani returns, finding enough at-bats for everyone will be one of Dave Roberts' biggest lineup challenges heading into October.

item.title: [Yardbarker] Dodgers have familiar Roki Sasaki spot for postseason
item.dc:creator: David Hill
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers hoped to keep pitcher Roki Sasaki stretched out as rotation depth as the postseason approaches. Instead, the Dodgers will begin their playoff plans for Sasaki as soon as he is activated from the Injured List. Sonja Chen of MLB.com reported that manager Dave Roberts said Sasaki will be available out of the bullpen beginning with their series against the Padres. That move to the bullpen will continue throughout of the postseason. Sasaki had worked strictly as a starter befo
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers hoped to keep pitcher Roki Sasaki stretched out as rotation depth as the postseason approaches. Instead, the Dodgers will begin their playoff plans for Sasaki as soon as he is activated from the Injured List.
Sonja Chen of MLB.com reported that manager Dave Roberts said Sasaki will be available out of the bullpen beginning with their series against the Padres. That move to the bullpen will continue throughout of the postseason.
Sasaki had worked strictly as a starter before landing on the IL. Although his overall performance - a 4.60 ERA and a 1.332 WHiP over his 119.1 innings - is still far from what was expected when he signed during the 2024-25 offseason, it is a step in the right direction. Sasaki struck out 117 batters with 48 walks in that time as he improved his K/9 and BB/9 rates over his rookie campaign.
The Dodgers are hoping that Sasaki can replicate his success from the 2025 postseason. He quickly became one of the few relievers Roberts could trust as the Dodgers marched to a second consecutive World Series title, moving into high-leverage situations while seeing action as their closer. He posted a 0.84 ERA and a 1.031 WHiP over his 10.2 innings in the 2025 postseason, recording three saves while striking out six batters with five walks.
In some ways, the Los Angeles Dodgers are still trying to figure out what they have in Sasaki. If he can replicate his success during the postseason, the Dodgers may be closer to having an answer.

item.title: [mlb.com] Postseason FAQ: What's next for the Red Sox?
item.dc:creator: Ian Browne

After losing in three games in the 2025 AL Wild Card Series to the Yankees at Yankee Stadium, the ending felt too abrupt. item.content:encoded:
Now, they have six regular-season games left to prepare for what is to come.
One big objective will be to get postseason baseball back to Fenway Park for the first time since 2021. After losing in three games in the 2025 AL Wild Card Series to the Yankees at Yankee Stadium, the ending felt too abrupt.
It has already been an improbable turnaround for the Red Sox, surging from 14 games under .500 on June 25 and getting to the postseason. There is a belief within the clubhouse that more magic can happen.
“I think we can make a run,” said rookie lefty Payton Tolle. “I think we’ve got the guys. I think we can get hot. We’re just going to continue to play the way that we play. That team baseball we’ve been playing. You play to get to the postseason and to give yourself a shot to go to the World Series.”
Without further ado, here are some key talking points heading into the playoffs.
What could the postseason roster look like?
C: Adley Rutschman, Connor Wong
1B: Willson Contreras
2B: Nick Sogard
SS: Trevor Story
3B: Caleb Durbin
UTIL: Isiah Kiner-Falefa, Mickey Gasper
OF: Jarren Duran, Ceddanne Rafaela, Wilyer Abreu, Braiden Ward
DH: Roman Anthony, Jahmai Jones
SP: Sonny Gray, Ranger Suarez, Payton Tolle
Bullpen: Aroldis Chapman, Garrett Whitlock, Tyron Guerrero, Erik Miller, Greg Weissert, Brayan Bello, Jake Bennett, Garrett Crochet, Tanner Houck
The most intriguing decision for the position-player roster surrounds whether to add Ward, who set the Triple-A Worcester record with 61 stolen bases this season, as a pinch-running specialist. Dave Roberts, anyone?
The bullpen situation also bears watching. Considering that Crochet hasn’t pitched since April 25 and Houck’s next appearance will be his first in the Majors since 2025, the club will monitor how both rehabbers are throwing before finalizing the roster. This could influence if the club carries Bennett as a reliever. Jovani Morán is another option from the left side.
When does the postseason begin?
For the Red Sox, the fun starts on Sept. 29, when interim manager Chad Tracy’s club participates in an AL Wild Card Series, with all games in the best-of-three series to be played on the road. The Yankees, unless they improbably take the AL East from the Rays, will be the Red Sox opponent in what will be yet another chapter in the richest rivalry in baseball. The only other scenario that can stave off another rivalry match would be the Red Sox slipping to the No. 6 seed. They lead the current No. 6 seed, the White Sox, by four games.
How have the Red Sox performed against the Yankees this season?
Last year, Boston’s hopes of getting a playoff game at Fenway Park for the first time since ‘21 ended when the team lost Game 3 of the Wild Card Series to … the Yankees in the Bronx. So, yes, this would be a rematch between the rivals. In a form befitting the rivalry, the regular-season series swayed back and forth, with New York ultimately taking seven of the 13 head-to-head encounters.
The Yankees swept the Red Sox at Fenway from April 21-23 in what wound up being Alex Cora’s last home series managing Boston. Fast forward to the Bronx from June 5-7, and the sides split, with the middle game getting postponed due to rain. For the Red Sox, their entire season started to turn around with a four-game sweep at Fenway from June 25-28. And for the Yankees, home field for this potential series was essentially wrapped up when they took three out of four from the Sox at the end of August to clinch the season series.
Will Aaron Judge be active for the Wild Card Series?
Judge’s potential participation in the series will be a huge focal point. The Yankees’ captain, limited to 66 games this season, was recently placed on the injured list again with a right calf strain. Though the Yankees have played more games without Judge than with him, his absence could make a difference for Boston.
What happens in the unlikely scenario the Red Sox slip from the No. 5 seed to the No. 6 spot?
In that case, the Red Sox would play the division champion with the worst record, which at this point would be whoever emerges victorious in a shaky AL West.
Which health situations should be monitored as the regular season winds down?
Where to start? There are many to choose from.
Contreras suffered a badly bruised knuckle between his right ring finger and pinkie when he was hit by a pitch on Sept. 17. He admitted he will be out for “days,” but hopes to be back before the postseason. It was a good sign that Contreras was able to grip a bat and take some swings on Sunday.
All eyes will be on Crochet to see if it’s possible to activate him for the playoffs as a reliever even though he hasn’t pitched since April 25 due to left shoulder inflammation.
Rafaela, the Red Sox's All-Star center fielder, has been out since Sept. 3 with a right quadriceps strain but should return before the regular season ends.
How does the rotation line up for the Red Sox?
If not for the near season-long loss of Crochet to this point, the Game 1 starter wouldn’t be in question. Tracy reordered his rotation for the upcoming series, going with Tolle on Tuesday against the Guardians, followed by Gray on Wednesday and Suarez on Thursday. Could this be the same order the Sox open the playoffs with? Tracy isn’t ready to reveal those plans yet.
How much postseason experience does Boston’s projected roster have?
Contreras and Chapman both won World Series rings while playing for the 2016 Cubs. Chapman added another one with the Rangers in ‘23. Kiner-Falefa was with Toronto last season, meaning he got to play in the epic Dodgers-Blue Jays World Series, losing one of the most dramatic Game 7s ever.
Rutschman played in five postseason games during his time with the Orioles, but none beyond the Division Series. Several players in Boston’s young core got their first taste of postseason experience last year in Abreu, Rafaela and Duran. Durbin went to the NLCS with the Brewers in ‘25. Houck and Whitlock are the only players remaining on the Boston team that came two wins from making the World Series in ‘21. Veteran shortstop Story had a solid Wild Card Series in the Bronx last year.
Suarez (4-1, 1.48 ERA in 11 outings, eight starts) had his share of October moments in Philadelphia, and Gray has a 3.26 ERA in six career playoff starts.

item.title: [thebiglead.com] Tarik Skubal leaves Dodgers temporarily for personal reasons 1 day after start against Giants
item.dc:creator: Miracle Dimwesh
item.description: Tarik Skubal has been one of the Los Angeles Dodgers’ biggest additions this season, but the veteran left-hander will now step away from the team temporarily. The Dodgers placed Skubal on the bereavement list Sunday, one day after he started against the San Francisco Giants. Manager Dave Roberts announced the move, according to The Athletic’s Fabian Ardaya. Skubal is expected to be away from the team for a few days. The Dodgers will adjust their pitching plans while he handles a personal matter.
item.content:encoded:
Tarik Skubal has been one of the Los Angeles Dodgers’ biggest additions this season, but the veteran left-hander will now step away from the team temporarily.
The Dodgers placed Skubal on the bereavement list Sunday, one day after he started against the San Francisco Giants. Manager Dave Roberts announced the move, according to The Athletic’s Fabian Ardaya.
Skubal is expected to be away from the team for a few days. The Dodgers will adjust their pitching plans while he handles a personal matter.
Tarik Skubal leaves Dodgers after Giants start
The timing comes immediately after Skubal’s latest start. He worked five innings against the Giants on Saturday, allowing eight hits, four earned runs and two walks while striking out three.
The Dodgers still won 10-4, with Mookie Betts going 4-for-4 and Will Smith adding a home run. Skubal received the win despite allowing four earned runs in the outing.
The start came during an important stretch for the Dodgers, who are already looking toward their postseason rotation. Skubal has given Los Angeles another frontline option since joining the club from Detroit.
His temporary absence, however, will force the Dodgers to make a short-term adjustment.
Dodgers turn to Emmet Sheehan
Emmet Sheehan is expected to step back into the Dodgers’ pitching plans Sunday. The right-hander provides another option as Los Angeles manages its rotation while Skubal is away.
The Dodgers have enough pitching depth to cover a short absence. Yoshinobu Yamamoto remains in the rotation, while Blake Snell has returned from the injured list.
Los Angeles has also already secured the NL West, giving the club some flexibility with its pitching plans. That could allow the Dodgers to avoid putting extra pressure on Skubal to return immediately.
Still, his availability will matter once the postseason begins. Skubal has been an important part of the Dodgers’ rotation since the trade, and the team will want him ready for October.
For now, the Dodgers will move forward without their ace for the next few days. The focus will be on Skubal’s return timeline and how Los Angeles adjusts its pitching plans in his absence.

item.title: [Dodger Blue] Dodgers have high expectations but cautious plan for Andy Pages
item.dc:creator: Matt Borelli
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are set to welcome back several key contributors this week, with Andy Pages expected to return for Tuesday’s series opener against the San Diego Padres. Pages won’t go on a Minor League rehab assignment before rejoining the Dodgers because of how late it is in the season, so he has six games to prepare for the playoffs. While live at-bats will be important to help him get back to game speed, the team plans to be cautious with his immediate workload. “So we have obviously,
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are set to welcome back several key contributors this week, with Andy Pages expected to return for Tuesday’s series opener against the San Diego Padres.
Pages won’t go on a Minor League rehab assignment before rejoining the Dodgers because of how late it is in the season, so he has six games to prepare for the playoffs. While live at-bats will be important to help him get back to game speed, the team plans to be cautious with his immediate workload.
“So we have obviously, assuming he gets back on Tuesday, then there’s six in a row, and that seems pretty aggressive,” manager Dave Roberts explained.
“So I think that we do want to get him as many at-bats as possible, but we have to make sure that his legs are under him, feeling good, so we don’t go backward or get injured in that respect. So it is going to be a balancing act, and just keeping a keen eye on Andy for sure.”
Pages has been on the 10-day injured list since Aug. 22 due to a left hand fracture. He underwent a procedure that involved inserting a screw into his left hand to accelerate the recovery process without extending the recovery timeline.
Pages was in the midst of a career year prior to landing on the IL and consistently put together quality at-bats for the Dodgers. Roberts expects more of the same when the 25-year-old returns, even if he initially gets off to a slow start following the long layoff.
“Yeah, I think I’m expecting good at-bats,” Roberts said. “I can’t speak to the performance. I think I just want him to have good at-bats. I’m not sure where he’s going to hit, somewhere in middle to the bottom, I think for me. But yeah, I don’t know. I think I’m waiting just like you guys are waiting to see how it looks.”
Pages provides even more value to the Dodgers with his elite defense in center field. Even in the event he struggles at the plate, Roberts believes he has a higher floor than most players because of his arm and glove.
“The defense is a big reason why he’s still a valuable player, even coming off the IL with the uncertainty of the offense, which we’ll still bet on. But playing at premium position and playing it well is hugely important,” Roberts said.
Andy Pages’ unique recovery
Pages first began hitting off a tee before progressing to swings off a pitching machine. More recently, he logged at-bats against the Trajekt machine.
In a perfect world, Pages would face live pitching before returning to the Dodgers. But with not many arms available, Roberts indicated the team feels comfortable activating the 2026 All-Star without those additional reps.

item.title: [True Blue LA] Emmet Sheehan on a hot streak: ‘My confidence stayed the same the whole time’
item.dc:creator: Eric Stephen
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Emmet Sheehan continued his late-season hot streak with another strong outing on Sunday against the San Francisco Giants, with nine strikeouts in 5 1/3 innings, allowing only a single and a walk. “I’ve loved the version of Emmet we’ve seen the last three outings,” manager Dave Roberts said Sunday. “He’s been fantastic.” Sheehan in three starts over the last two weeks since rejoining the Dodgers has allowed only one run in 17 innings, with 24 strikeouts against only three walks.
