item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Emmet Sheehan continued his late-season hot streak with another strong outing on Sunday against the San Francisco Giants, with nine strikeouts in 5 1/3 innings, allowing only a single and a walk.
“I’ve loved the version of Emmet we’ve seen the last three outings,” manager Dave Roberts said Sunday. “He’s been fantastic.”
Sheehan in three starts over the last two weeks since rejoining the Dodgers has allowed only one run in 17 innings, with 24 strikeouts against only three walks. It came after spending most of August in Triple-A.
“I don’t know if I proved anything to myself,” Sheehan said. “It was more just getting a couple of things right, and I’m in a much better spot now.”
Sheehan was in the Dodgers rotation from opening day through August 2, when he allowed three home runs and five runs in a loss to the Boston Red Sox. Twenty starts into the season, Sheehan wasn’t getting results (5.29 ERA, belying his 4.00 xERA), and was having issues holding his velocity throughout his starts. He was optioned to Oklahoma City the next day.
That time in the minors was productive for Sheehan. After a planned shortened outing in which he allowed two runs in 2/3 of an inning, Sheehan struck out 24 over three starts with one run allowed in 17 1/3 innings. That earned him a Pacific Coast League pitcher of the week award and pitcher of the month honors for August.
“My confidence stayed the same the whole time. I knew the coaches down there were going to help me, and I was going to get right,” Sheehan said. “I took that approach going into it. I wasn’t helping the team here, so I needed that a little bit. I feel like in a good spot.”
“We’ve seen confidence. When you’re essentially fighting for your life, to create an opportunity for yourself, that’s what I see. There’s urgency,” Roberts said. “I like the way he’s trusting his stuff, he’s in a good spot physically, and the performance has been fantastic.”
One tweak Sheehan made was throwing his curveball more. In his last three outings with the Dodgers, he threw the curve 21.9 percent of the time, up from his 12.3 percent over the course of the season.
“It’s something, Connor [McGuiness, assistant pitching coach], Mark [Prior, pitching coach], and I and the coaches down at Triple-A have been working on a lot is expanding the front-to-back game with the fastball and the curveball,” Sheehan said. “Some guys ended up throughout the season sitting more mid-speed, slider, changeup on me. I think having that change of speeds has been really important.
On Sunday against San Francisco, Sheehan induced 15 of his 18 swinging strikes on his fastball and curveball and finished off five of his nine strikeouts with those two pitches.
Sheehan’s first 26 outings this year were starts, but on Sunday he followed an opener, at the very least getting him oriented about his possible relief role in the postseason. After three solid months in the rotation last season, Sheehan pitched in relief in October, with mixed results (8.59 ERA, 13 hits and five walks in 7 1/3 innings). He allowed runs in each of his four appearances, though rebounded with 2 2/3 scoreless innings in extras in the marathon Game 3, when got three outs with two strikeouts in a scoreless outing in the seventh and eighth innings of Game 7.
“The routine of everything can be a little hard to adjust to, so having that experience helps a lot. Getting back into that, I know what I need to do to be ready to go in the game,” Sheehan said. “Execution was off in the first couple, but then I felt better as it went on.”
Sheehan returned Sunday when Tarik Skubal went on the bereavement list, and the plan is for Sheehan to be optioned back to Triple-A, perhaps as early as Tuesday when Roki Sasaki is likely activated from the injured list straight into a high-leverage relief role.
Roberts on Sunday said the plan is for Sheehan to start on Saturday in the Triple-A championship game, provided Oklahoma City beats Las Vegas in the best-of-3 PCL championship starting Tuesday. But after that, Sheehan will almost certainly be on the playoff roster. Most likely he’ll be in a relief role, but that might depend on how Blake Snell progresses over the next two weeks from his left groin tightness.
“After [Sheehan] makes that last start, we’ll evaluate where we are as a staff,” Roberts said.
“Whatever role they want me to do going forward, I’m ready to do it,” Sheehan said. “It was nice to get that experience coming out of the pen.”

item.title: [Dodger Blue] Dodgers don't plan to hold anything back with Shohei Ohtani
item.dc:creator: Matt Borelli
item.description: Shohei Ohtani made significant progress toward returning to the Los Angeles Dodgers over the weekend as he looks to return from left knee and right arm/bicep trouble that has thrown his 2026 season well off course. Ohtani took 30 to 40 swings off the Trajekt machine after recently hitting against a coach. He then ran the bases on the field with Dodgers strength coach Travis Smith overseeing the work. Ohtani is eligible to be activated off the 15-day injured list on Sept. 23, and manager Dave Rob
item.content:encoded:
Shohei Ohtani made significant progress toward returning to the Los Angeles Dodgers over the weekend as he looks to return from left knee and right arm/bicep trouble that has thrown his 2026 season well off course.
Ohtani took 30 to 40 swings off the Trajekt machine after recently hitting against a coach. He then ran the bases on the field with Dodgers strength coach Travis Smith overseeing the work.
Ohtani is eligible to be activated off the 15-day injured list on Sept. 23, and manager Dave Roberts believes that remains a viable possibility.
“Still up in the air, but that’s our hope,” Roberts said.
If Ohtani returns on Wednesday against the San Diego Padres, he will have only five regular season games to prepare for the playoffs. He won’t go on a Minor League rehab assignment due to it being so late in the season.
“Absolutely. He’ll need those live at-bats,” Roberts said when asked if he plans to play Ohtani through the end of the regular season.
That’s going to represent a change from when Ohtani was last active. He missed four consecutive games and then was out of the lineup again one day after returning on Sept. 7. That wound up leading to the stint on the injured list.
Prior to Ohtani going on the IL, he had long appeared compromised at the plate because of his lingering injuries. Roberts conceded that Ohtani likely isn’t back to full strength but said he should be able to manage any discomfort for the remainder of the season.
“Discomfort he can play through. I would say pain-free. I think there’s a difference between discomfort and pain,” Roberts began.
“Is it 100%? Probably not. Is it better than it was a week ago? Yes. Honestly, I think that’s a better question for Shohei, to get more specifics. But I do think when he’s activated, it’s going to be the best physical place he’s been in quite some time.”
Shohei Ohtani’s role
When Ohtani does return, he will be limited to designated hitter duties as the team has all but ruled him out of pitching again this year.
“Disappointing, but I want to make sure that when I look back on this season, I use it as a learning experience and make sure I use it as something to improve upon for next season,” Ohtani said through interpreter Will Ireton earlier this month.
While it’s not the outcome that Ohtani hoped for, he understands his importance as a hitter and will try to do everything he can to lead the Dodgers to a third consecutive World Series title.

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Mookie Betts' sudden revival could be Dodgers' secret weapon in securing three-peat
item.dc:creator: Brandon Glick
item.description: The death of Mookie Betts at the plate appears to have been greatly exaggerated. The eight-time All-Star certainly won't be able to consider his 2026 campaign alongside some of his historic performances from years past, but he's put together another strong season after a calamitous start. Specifically since August 17, he's been one of the best hitters in all of baseball. item.content:encoded:
The death of Mookie Betts at the plate appears to have been greatly exaggerated. The eight-time All-Star certainly won't be able to consider his 2026 campaign alongside some of his historic performances from years past, but he's put together another strong season after a calamitous start.
Specifically since August 17, he's been one of the best hitters in all of baseball. He leads the Los Angeles Dodgers in all three triple-slash categories (.336/.427/.611), wRC+ (183), home runs (seven), RBI (27), and fWAR (2.0) from that point forward, emerging at a time when the team has gotten all of 71 plate appearances (and a 101 wRC+) from Shohei Ohtani.
Betts isn't a "secret weapon" by traditional standards; his MVP credentials and three World Series rings would certainly beg to differ. But after he struggled mightily a year ago and then followed that up with an even worse encore at the beginning of 2026, having him healthy and in his best groove in years could be the deciding factor in the Dodgers' quest for a three-peat.
Mookie Betts has elevated his own floor and with it, the Dodgers' ceiling
The Dodgers are hardly hurting for production, ranking third in the league in runs scored since mid-August. Even without Ohtani, they can batter opposing pitching staffs with their depth, especially now that Kyle Tucker finally looks interested in participating in this group project.
But more than a rejuvenated Tucker or red-hot Teoscar Hernández, there's something special about Betts in particular getting this hot. He's the fourth-longest tenured player on the roster, surpassed by only Max Muncy and Will Smith among position players. He's been around for each of the three recent championships, posting a cumulative OPS over .800 in those playoff runs.
One of the most selfless superstars you'll ever find, there's a "you go, we go" aura that orbits Betts, especially now that he's reclaimed his rightful spot atop the batting order as Dave Roberts' leadoff hitter. His all-around talents lengthen the lineup to a tremendous degree, something opposing pitchers will really feel once Ohtani is back in the fold.
It's not all perfect, of course. His hard-hit rate even during this hot streak is well below the figures he'd post in his prime, and he's still hitting a few too many balls on the ground. Naturally, all of his expected stats during this stretch fall shy of his actual results, including significant disparities in his slugging percentage (.611 compared to a .458 xSLG) and wOBA (.443 compared to a .374 xwOBA).
Those expected metrics are still leaps and bounds better than we got earlier this season, though, and that's the real takeaway here. Even if Betts can't keep this MVP-caliber charade going through all of October, he's clearly found a more stable baseline level of performance that can still help the Dodgers win.

item.title: [New York Post] Roki Sasaki to return to Dodgers this week with a twist
item.dc:creator: Dylan Hernandez
item.description: Will Roki Sasaki again be the Dodgers’ closer in the playoffs? The Dodgers have created a pathway to make that possible, as manager Dave Roberts said that Sasaki will be moved into the bullpen when he is activated from the injured list this week. Sasaki has pitched in 23 games this season, every one of them starts. A blister on his pitching hand has sidelined him since Aug. 27, but Roberts said he expected him to be activated during an upcoming three-game series against the Padres that starts on
item.content:encoded:
Will Roki Sasaki again be the Dodgers’ closer in the playoffs?
The Dodgers have created a pathway to make that possible, as manager Dave Roberts said that Sasaki will be moved into the bullpen when he is activated from the injured list this week.
Sasaki has pitched in 23 games this season, every one of them starts. A blister on his pitching hand has sidelined him since Aug. 27, but Roberts said he expected him to be activated during an upcoming three-game series against the Padres that starts on Tuesday.
The Dodgers had refrained from turning Sasaki into a reliever up to this point because of concerns over their starting rotation. Blake Snell departed from his most recent start after one inning because of a tight groin, but the two-time Cy Young Award winner has since not experienced any problems in that area.
The team believes it has four healthy starters in Snell, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal and Tyler Glasnow. Emmet Sheehan figures to be the rotation’s new insurance policy, as Sheehan has allowed only one run in 17 innings pitched this month.
Roberts said he doesn’t plan to use Sasaki as a quasi-starter who pitches four or five innings following an opener.
Asked if Sasaki would be used in late-inning, high-leverage situations, Roberts replied, “I trust Roki in any situation. I would say probably start a clean inning, but, yeah.”
Could he close?
“It won’t be the ninth inning the first time,” Roberts said.
But Roberts acknowledged there was a chance Sasaki could end up in that role.
Sasaki became the Dodgers’ closer last year by default, as the team didn’t have any other options. He saved three games in the postseason.
His move to the bullpen last year came after he missed 4 ½ months because of shoulder problems. He agreed to try pitching in relief under the condition the Dodgers let him start again the next season.
Sasaki is 5-5 with a 4.70 earned-run average this year, but was 2-0 with a 3.05 ERA in the seven starts he made after the All-Star break.
The Dodgers started this season counting on $69-million free agent addition Edwin Diaz to be their closer, but the three-time All-Star has endured a nightmare of a season that has included two IL stints. In Diaz’s absence, Tanner Scott has served as the team’s primary ninth-inning option and has performed well. However, Scott has posted a 4.97 ERA over his last 14 games.

item.title: [True Blue LA] Dodgers Week 26: Back in the postseason saddle again
item.dc:creator: Eric Stephen
item.description: The Dodgers are taking advantage of the schedule in front of them, with 14 wins in 19 September games, including winning the last 10 in a row at home. This week that meant beating the Reds three times in four games in Cincinnati, then returning to Los Angeles to sweep the Giants. They went with a two-way under the Cincinnati skyline, first clinching a postseason berth on Monday, tying the Atlanta Braves record with 14 straight postseasons, followed by winning their fifth straight National League
item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers are taking advantage of the schedule in front of them, with 14 wins in 19 September games, including winning the last 10 in a row at home. This week that meant beating the Reds three times in four games in Cincinnati, then returning to Los Angeles to sweep the Giants.
They went with a two-way under the Cincinnati skyline, first clinching a postseason berth on Monday, tying the Atlanta Braves record with 14 straight postseasons, followed by winning their fifth straight National League West title and 13 out of 14 on Thursday.
Entering the final week of the season, the Dodgers can clinch a bye week with a magic number of three over the Braves.
Batter of the week
Kyle Tucker is starting to turn things around at the plate, and followed up an excellent series the previous weekend in Miami with nine hits in 20 at-bats, with three home runs and two doubles, with six walks and just one strikeout.
Honorable mention goes to Mookie Betts, who tied a Dodgers record with three doubles on Saturday, part of a stretch of three consecutive games with at least three hits. Will Smith found his power again with two home runs and a double, and Alex Freeland reached base eight times in 14 trips to the plate, including a home run and a double.
Pitcher of the week
Yoshinobu Yamamoto pitched seven scoreless innings with seven strikeouts to beat the Reds on Tuesday, his third straight seven-inning start in September. Yamamoto this season has allowed zero or one run in 14 of his 27 starts.
Honorable mention goes to Justin Wrobleski, who retired all nine batters he faced with three strikeouts while starting Thursday’s division clincher in Cincinnati, and to Landon Knack, who got the win in that game with four scoreless innings in relief. Also to Emmet Sheehan, who continued his strong six-week run with nine strikouts in 5 1/3 scoreless frames on Sunday.
Week 26 results
6-1 record
39 runs scored (5.57 per game)
16 runs allowed (2.29 per game)
.836 pythagorean win percentage
Year to date
96-60 record
780 runs scored (5.00 per game)
587 runs allowed (3.76 per game)
.627 pythagorean win percentage (98-58)
Miscellany
Half a hundred: The Dodgers have won 10 games in a row at home, and Sunday’s win was their 50th win at Dodger Stadium this season. That’s six straight years with 50 wins at home, plus seven straight full seasons dating back to 2019. Since moving into Dodger Stadium, the Dodgers won 50 home games 12 times in 51 full seasons through 2014. But since 2015, they’ve won at least 50 games at home 10 times in 11 full seasons.
A crowded 10-K: Tyler Glasnow beat the Giants on Friday with a strong six innings, including 10 strikeouts. Glasnow is the eighth different Dodgers pitcher with a 10-strikeout game this season, the most in franchise history. No other MLB team this year has more than five such pitchers.
Parliamentary procedure: After making the All-Star team as a starter with the Kansas City Royals in 2025, left-hander Kris Bubic was on the 60-day injured list when the Dodgers acquired him just ahead of the August 3 trade deadline. Now he’s pitching in relief, angling for a spot on the postseason roster. With his appearance on Wednesday, Bubic became the 33rd different Dodgers pitcher used this season. So far, Bubic has four strikeouts in 2 2/3 innings in three appearances. “It’s just funk,” manager Dave Roberts said Sunday of Bubic. “It’s nothing overpowering, but there’s just funky swings, soft contact. I see him as a neutral pitcher, gets left and right out. I like those converted starters, because he knows how to navigate lineups.”
A quirk: The division clincher Thursday in Cincinnati was an 8-2 win, then came four home runs in the eighth inning Friday on the 20th anniversary of the 4+1 Game for another 8-2 triumph. That was the first time in Dodgers history they’ve won consecutive games by an 8-2 score.
Transactions
Monday: The fresh arm express was busy this week, beginning with Emmet Sheehan getting optioned the day after pitching six scoreless innings, in favor of Paul Gervase.
Monday: One day after a rare bad outing, Edgardo Henriquez was placed on the injured list with low back discomfort, ending his regular season and putting his playoff availability in question. Bobby Miller returned from Triple-A.
Wednesday: Trade deadline acquisition Kris Bubic was activated off the 60-day IL to make his Dodgers debut in relief, the team’s 33rd pitcher of the season. Gervase was optioned and Ryan Ward was designated for assignment.
Thursday: Miller was sent back to Oklahoma City, and Landon Knack was called up to pitch four scoreless innings in relief in the division clincher in Cincinnati.
Sunday: Sheehan got the call back up to the Dodgers, with Tarik Skubal placed on the bereavement list. Kyle Hurt was also called up, with Seth Halvorsen optioned.

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers top prospect Josue De Paula recently made his MLB debut with LA.
He’s had a few very solid moments at the plate, and he’s showcased his impressive plate discipline with an ability to put the ball in play and drive it to the opposite side of the field.
De Paula is still very young, so there’s plenty of time to develop in the coming years, but it’s been a welcome sign thus far in his first handful of MLB action.
Recently, Josue De Paula shared an honest message about dealing with critics to Dodgers reporter Fabian Ardaya.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Get Major Andy Pages Update Ahead of Padres Series
Josue De Paula Shares Honest Message
Per Ardaya, here is what Josue De Paula had to say about critics calling out his defense:
“I know that’s a big area of improvement for me,” said De Paula. “I know I got a lot of hate on it. I’m that type: if I get hate on it, I’m going to focus on it more. So I’m gonna shut a lot of people up with my defense very soon. It’s gonna take some time.”
Even manager Dave Roberts said that De Paula still has a lot of development to do in the outfield, but it’s been clear De Paula’s defense isn’t the reason he’s in the show.
Ardaya notes that De Paula could have a full-time role with the Dodgers if he shores up his defensive ability:
“The list of helpful voices kept growing over the first 10 days of De Paula’s big-league career. His bat could be special, but De Paula’s path to impacting the 2027 Dodgers becomes a lot easier if he proves he can handle the corner outfield. Mookie Betts, a six-time Gold Glove winner in right field, gave him pointers on how to shag fly balls. Manager Dave Roberts, who spent 10 years patrolling big-league outfields, goes out of his way to ensure De Paula emphasizes the details.”
With all the stars on the Dodgers roster, De Paula’s development is in good hands.
More MLB on Heavy: New York Mets Trade Pitch Offloads Mark Vientos to Pirates
Josue De Paula’s Rookie Campaign Thus Far
Josue De Paula has played in just 10 games for LA, and across his first 38 MLB plate appearances, he’s batted .286 with 10 walks, eight hits, six runs, one home run, and 3 doubles.
Those are very solid numbers to start your MLB career, and especially as a top prospect.
Here is some of De Paula’s prospect bio, per MiLB.com:
“De Paula draws comparisons to a slightly smaller but more athletic version of Yordan Alvarez, thanks to his precocious combination of swing decisions and exit velocities. He offered at just 14 percent of pitches outside the strike zone last season — by comparison, Juan Soto led the Majors with a 16 percent rate — and is supremely comfortable working deep counts in order to find pitches he can punish.”
Yordan Alvarez? The frontrunner for 2026 AL MVP? Not a bad comparison. The future looks bright for Josue De Paula thus far.

item.title: [Dodger Blue] Josue De Paula responds to criticism about defense with bold prediction
item.dc:creator: Blake Williams
item.description: Josue De Paula has been everything the Los Angeles Dodgers could have hoped for in the batter’s box during since getting called up for his MLB debut. Since being added onto the Dodgers roster to replace Shohei Ohtani as the everyday designated hitter, De Paula has shown off his patience, ability to take a quality at-bat, and power and speed combination. The sky is the limit for De Paula’s offensive capabilities, and that’s what carried him to the MLB level. But his defense in the outfield is a m
item.content:encoded:
Josue De Paula has been everything the Los Angeles Dodgers could have hoped for in the batter’s box during since getting called up for his MLB debut.
Since being added onto the Dodgers roster to replace Shohei Ohtani as the everyday designated hitter, De Paula has shown off his patience, ability to take a quality at-bat, and power and speed combination. The sky is the limit for De Paula’s offensive capabilities, and that’s what carried him to the MLB level.
But his defense in the outfield is a major area of concern, and it’s part of the reason the Dodgers did not call De Paula up until needing a regular DH. As they look ahead to the postseason, De Paula is likely to be limited to being a bat off the bench, given his defensive struggles and the uptick of production from Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker.
However, De Paula knows he needs to improve in the outfield, and he’s made it a focus during his first stint at the MLB level.
“Every day. I know that’s a big area of improvement for me, and I know I’ve got a lot of hate on it,” De Paula said. “I’m the type that if I get hate on it, I’m going to focus on it more. I’m going to shut a lot of people up with my defense very soon.”
De Paula has spent time before every game practicing his defense, working with Dodgers coaches to become more of a usable option in the outfield. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts has taken notice of that, and issued a challenge to De Paula.
“Well, it’s clear he needs to improve on his defense,” Roberts said. “How do you shut people up? You perform better. You practice hard, and that’s how you do it. My challenge to him is to be a complete baseball player, and not just to be a hitter. So he’s putting a lot of good work with Dino every day, and so I welcome that.”
Josue De Paula praises Dodgers teammates
De Paula became the first position player promoted from Double-A by Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman, creating lofty expectations for himself.
The 21-year-old has felt prepared to meet the challenge of playing in the Majors head-on and credits his Dodgers teammates for creating an environment conducive to letting him play freely.
“Probably the biggest is takeaway is it’s basically the same game, just around different people,” De Paula said on SportsNet LA. “But one thing I didn’t expect was this team to be so cool. Like, all the players, the way they accepted me, the way they greeted me, making me feel comfortable. It put me in a better position to be me.”

item.title: [Yardbarker] 'Wouldn’t Have Won the World Series': Shohei Ohtani’s Impact on Dodgers Runs Deeper Than Expected as Dave Roberts Reveals Why
item.dc:creator: Srijanee Chakraborty
item.description: Dave Roberts manages one of the most star-studded rosters in the league, and the Los Angeles Dodgers play like one. But according to Roberts, their impressive championship success is not shaped by something we can see on a box score. It runs deeper than the analytics and has everything to do with their MVP Shohei Ohtani and ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto. According to the Dodgers manager, Ohtani and Yamamoto brought a level of discipline and intentionality inside the clubhouse that set a benchmark for t
item.content:encoded:
Dave Roberts manages one of the most star-studded rosters in the league, and the Los Angeles Dodgers play like one. But according to Roberts, their impressive championship success is not shaped by something we can see on a box score.
It runs deeper than the analytics and has everything to do with their MVP Shohei Ohtani and ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
According to the Dodgers manager, Ohtani and Yamamoto brought a level of discipline and intentionality inside the clubhouse that set a benchmark for the entire team. It did not go unnoticed by the players.
Roberts recalled on the611podcast that Dodgers veteran Mookie Betts also felt the same.
“Mookie told me a couple of years ago, ‘Doc, we wouldn’t have won the World Series if it wasn’t for Shohei and Yamamoto’. And his point was the discipline that they had every single day,” said Roberts on the podcast.
“How they work with intention every single day, because what that made, it raised the level even higher for our guys. Yamamoto’s day-to-day is three to four hours of intentionality to prepare to throw a bullpen. Shohei is the same way. Roki is getting there, but his culture- that’s what they do.”
The Dodgers signed Ohtani and Yamamoto ahead of the 2024 season.
Ohtani signed the historic 10-year, $700 million contract, while Yamamoto agreed to a massive 12-year, $325 million deal. They proved that every million spent was worth it, as the Dodgers became the World Series champion in 2024 and again in 2025.
Ohtani’s three-homer, 10-strikeout performance in Game 4 of the NLCS, leading to the World Series, is one for the history books. In Game 2 of the 2024 World Series, Ohtani suffered a partial dislocation in his left shoulder while trying to steal a base. But showing incredible toughness, he returned in Game 3 to play against the New York Yankees.
It does not happen without intentionality, and Ohtani’s whole regimen is driven by it. Shotime runs by the clock; from sleeping to bullpen sessions, everything has a fixed schedule. He is Roberts’ “easiest player to manage.”
Last season, Ohtani finished Game 3 of the World Series by reaching base a record-setting 9 times, hitting 2 doubles and 2 homers. The two-way phenom ended the championship batting .333, with 3 homers and 5 RBIs.
Yamamoto was equally impressive.
During the 2024 Fall Classic, Yamamoto threw a one-hit, one-run game, pitching for six innings. In the following edition, he threw in three games and gave up 2 runs to the Toronto Blue Jays, logging a 1.02 ERA.
“When you’re talking about winning 11 games in October, I couldn’t believe more [that] it’s about people, and players you can bet on,” Roberts said on the podcast.
Ohtani and Yamamoto are the players Roberts bet on. Their success is defined by the discipline they rigorously maintain.
When Yamamoto arrived at the Dodgers clubhouse, he brought his own regimen that influenced others.
He relies on flexibility to generate momentum rather than brute strength. Apart from taking bullpen sessions like clockwork, Yamamoto also practices javelin throwing.
He follows a routine designed by his personal trainer and guru, Osamu Yada. Yamamoto also famously keeps a notebook in the dugout to jot down observations from the game. All these habits work together to make him successful.
Roberts also revealed how the presence of these Japanese players influenced the Americans.
“So now, when you get younger players that we have, or even American players that are veterans, they’re like, they’re doing it this intentional, this precise, and that’s the thing that, as a manager, I love,” noted Roberts.
“Because you don’t know where games are gonna go. Games are gonna get hot, and the pressure’s gonna get there. But you have to be able to default to kind of what you know. And that’s what, again, in baseball, can kind of default to doing things the right way.”
And to the Dodgers’ credit, they did not try to ignore the vastly unfamiliar culture. Rather, they chose to learn from it. Perhaps that mentality is what makes them champions.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 21: Andy Pages #44 of the Los Angeles Dodgers reacts between Dave Roberts #30 and Rafael Flores Jr. #43 of the Pittsburgh Pirates, after he was hit by a pitch, during the third inning at Dodger Stadium on August 21, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images)
The Los Angeles Dodgers are coming off a three-game sweep of the San Francisco Padres this past weekend.
LA, after clinching the NL West, is still looking to secure the NL’s No.2 seed with just six games left on the schedule. Next up for LA is a series with the San Diego Padres, who are rolling right now in MLB. The Dodgers have Monday off after a long stretch of games.
As the Dodgers gear up for a playoff run, they recently received a great piece of news regarding outfielder Andy Pages.
“Andy Pages will be activated before Tuesday’s game vs. SD, Dave Roberts said, with Shohei Ohtani “shortly” after. Roki Sasaki will be available out of the bullpen as Dodgers begin to plot out their October relief roles. Big week for a lot of guys, including Edwin Díaz.”
The MLB regular season has just one week left until the playoffs begin starting next week.
Getting Andy Pages back will be a huge boost for the Dodgers lineup, as he’s been enjoying a solid campaign and contributing heavily to the team’s offense.
GettyLOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA – AUGUST 15: Andy Pages #44 of the Los Angeles Dodgers reacts at the plate during the game against the Milwaukee Brewers at Dodger Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images)
Andy Pages injured his hand after being hit by a pitch about a month ago, which landed him on the IL.
LA obviously wants to take things slow with Pages to avoid further injury, but the consensus is that he is good to go after doing a lot of off-field hitting work.
A first-time MLB All-Star this season, Pages is batting .272 with 21 home runs, 25 doubles, 80 RBI, and an OPS+ of 117.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants, 3-1, on Sunday and improved to 96-60 on the year. They completed the series sweep of the divisional rivals and notched their fourth-straight win (and 14th of the last 17).
After Jack Dreyer took the start and allowed an earned run in the first inning, Emmet Sheehan pitched the next 5.1 frames and stole the show on the mound. He struck out nine, allowed one hit, one walk and no earned runs.
Offensively, Teoscar Hernndez, Freddie Freeman, Max Muncy and Josue De Paula each had a two-hit game. De Paula was 5-for-10 over the course of the series, just the first of hopefully many more at Dodger Stadium.
Ahead of the eventual victory, southpaw Tarik Skubal unfortunately had to be placed on the bereavement list. As he deals with his personal matter, it is likely that he will still make one more start (he is next scheduled for Sept. 26) before the postseason.
In other news, manager Dave Roberts made a somewhat surprising admission regarding superstar Mookie Betts. After hitting just .235 before the All-Star break, Betts has completely turned things around and looks like a more familiar version of himself, hitting .322 in his last 30 games.
"I couldn't tell you that I saw this," Roberts said on Saturday regarding Betts' turnaround. "But I just felt that he was stronger. He's worked hard on that. He looks great. He's not going to stop working, and just for it to come together has been great."
Finally, a Dodgers pitcher was demoted as part of the four-player roster move made on Sunday. The right-hander has an impressive 1.32 ERA across 26 games (27.1 innings) at the Triple-A level, but in 11 appearances with the Dodgers this season, he has an 8.10 ERA across 10 innings of work.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Kyle Tucker didn’t start on Sunday, one day after fouling a ball off his right knee, but the Dodgers right fielder insisted that he felt fine. This was more of a chance to pair a rest day for Tucker with Monday’s scheduled off day for the team.
“[The off day] wasn’t planned. I just felt that after he took one off the knee, this would have been 10 in a row for him,” manager Dave Roberts said Sunday. “He’s playing well, played a lot. It’s a chance to give him two days, then six in a row to finish the season.”
The injury was in a much higher spot on his leg than the right shin fracture that cost him two months on the injured list during the 2024 season while with the Houston Astros.
Tucker did pinch-hit in the eighth inning on Sunday, and he’s second on the Dodgers in games played (148), starts (141), and plate appearances (602), trailing only Freddie Freeman in all three categories. Tucker is playing the best baseball of his season at the moment with five home runs in his last 10 starts, hitting .417/.500/.972 since September 9.
Notes
Speaking of playing in the outfield on Tuesday, the Dodgers will likely activate center fielder Andy Pages off the injured list to play in the series opener against the San Diego Padres, after he missed the last 27 games after a fastball broke his left hand on August 21.
Pages at the end of this season will have two years, 155 days of major league service time and will be eligible for salary arbitration for the first time as a Super Two player, among the top 70 percent in service time among major leaguers with two years but not yet three years of service time. MLB Trade Rumors last week projected the cutoff for Super Two players this offseason to be two years, 134 days.
Longtime Dodgers third base coach Joey Amalfitano and knuckleballer Charlie Hough were honored on the field at Dodger Stadium prior to Sunday’s game as the 2026 winners of the the Tommy Lasorda I Bleed Dodger Blue Award. This is the fifth year of the award, timed close to Lasorda’s birthday, which is Tuesday.

item.dc:creator: Renzo Pocholo Salao

The Japanese slugger began hitting balls off a tee last week in preparation for a return to the lineup. The Athletic’s Fabian Ardaya reported Saturday that Ohtani will come off the injured list on Wednesday. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts told reporters that there’s “a
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers may be getting Shohei Ohtani back in the lineup before the MLB calendar turns to October.
The Dodgers placed Ohtani on the 15-day IL on Sept. 8 as he continues to deal with lingering knee and bicep injuries. The Japanese slugger began hitting balls off a tee last week in preparation for a return to the lineup.
The Athletic’s Fabian Ardaya reported Saturday that Ohtani will come off the injured list on Wednesday. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts told reporters that there’s “a good chance” Ohtani gets activated for a return either on Wednesday or Thursday.
Ohtani reportedly swung off a Trajekt Arc machine, which is expected to be the closest he’ll get to facing live pitching before returning to the Dodgers’ lineup. He also managed “between 30 to 40 swings” in the batting cage during L.A.’s win over the San Francisco Giants.
If Ohtani returns on Wednesday, the four-time MVP would have only five regular-season games to get his bat going again before the playoffs. He has only had three at-bats since going 0-for-4 in the Dodgers’ Sept. 2 loss to the St. Louis Cardinals.
Ohtani has all but abandoned any hopes of him pitching again this season, which means the Dodgers likely won’t be benefiting from any ridiculous two-way performances as Shohei had last year.
How quickly Shohei begins to look like himself again at the plate make the difference in October as the Dodgers go for a historic three-peat.

item.title: [sbsun.com] Emmet Sheehan strengthens postseason case as Dodgers sweep Giants
item.dc:creator: Bill Plunkett
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Hiding behind that 5.00 ERA Emmet Sheehan toted around for much of the season might have been a valuable postseason piece. Sheehan allowed just one hit in 5⅓ scoreless innings on Sunday afternoon as the Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants, 3-1, to complete a three-game sweep. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Hiding behind that 5.00 ERA Emmet Sheehan toted around for much of the season might have been a valuable postseason piece.
Sheehan allowed just one hit in 5⅓ scoreless innings on Sunday afternoon as the Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants, 3-1, to complete a three-game sweep.
Sheehan retired 16 of the 18 batters he faced, allowing just one single and walking one while striking out nine.
“I’ve loved the version we’ve seen of Emmet the last three outings,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. “He’s been fantastic.
“We’ve seen confidence. We’ve seen when you’re essentially fighting for your life to create an opportunity for yourself. That’s what I see. There’s urgency. I like the way that he’s trusting his stuff. He’s in a good spot physically, and you know the performance has been fantastic.”
The outing was Sheehan’s third consecutive outstanding performance this month as he has bounced between Triple-A and the majors. It cemented a spot in the Dodgers’ postseason bullpen after a rough season for the 26-year-old right-hander – an outcome that did not seem likely when he was demoted to Triple-A in early August.
“I don’t know that I proved anything to myself. It was just getting a couple things right and I think I’m in a much better spot now,” Sheehan said.
“My confidence stayed the same the whole time. I knew the coaches down there were going to help me and I was going to get right. I took that approach going into it. I wasn’t helping the team here so I needed that a little bit.”
Sheehan has been called up for two starts this month and pitched in ‘bulk’ following Jack Dreyer as an opener on Sunday. Sheehan carried a 5.29 ERA into September after 20 starts for the Dodgers that landed him back in the minors.
In his three September outings, though, Sheehan has shown rediscovered fastball command after working on his delivery in Triple-A. He has allowed just one run in 17 innings, holding hitters to a .105 average (6 for 57) with 24 strikeouts and three walks. After giving up 20 home runs in those first 20 starts, he has allowed just one in his 17 September innings.
If his confidence didn’t need repair, his delivery and pitch mix needed some work.
Now two years removed from Tommy John surgery, Sheehan was thrown by not quite having recovered all of his fastball velocity this year. When he chased those extra miles per hour, it was counterproductive. He has become more comfortable at 94-95 mph now.
“I think it’s a few things,” he said Sunday. “Definitely … being more comfortable in my delivery, being out there staying free and easy with everything, not trying to do too much. Instead of saying, ‘I need 97 here.’ It’s more like ‘If I hit my spot, he’s not going to hit it.’”
They haven’t. Sheehan has gotten 50 swings-and-misses in his three outings this month, nearly half of them (24) on his reborn four-seam fastball. He also got six on his curveball on Sunday.
“That’s something that (assistant pitching coach) Connor (McGuinness), (pitching coach) Mark (Prior) and I and the coaches down in Triple-A have been working on is just expanding the front-to-back game with the fastball and the curveball,” Sheehan said. “I think some guys ended up throughout the season sitting mid-speed, slider-changeup, on me. Having that change of speeds the last couple has been very important.”
The Dodgers moved Sheehan to the bullpen for the postseason last October and saw him as a big weapon in that role. The results were mixed, however, in part because of some pitch tipping issues which Sheehan said have been addressed. He will be wiser this time around, he said.
“Definitely,” Sheehan said. “I think the routine of everything can be a little bit hard to adjust to right away. So having that experience helps a lot. Just getting back into that, I know what I need to do to get ready to go into the game.”
The Dodgers gave him a little bit of a test drive by using Dreyer as an ‘opener’ before him. The Giants scratched out one run in the first inning against Dreyer when he walked leadoff man Jonah Cox. Cox moved to second base on a wild pickoff attempt by Dreyer, stole third and scored on Victor Bericoto’s RBI single. The Giants had just one more hit in the game.
“I think that obviously there’s a 97 that plays better, but 94-95 commanded still misses bats,” Roberts said of Sheehan, who will rejoin Oklahoma City for the Triple-A playoffs this week before returning to the Dodgers for the postseason. “That’s one part of it. The other part of it is holding the velocity. And so, for me, the last three or four since he’s been back here, he’s held those 94s and 95s for the, call it 85 pitches.”
The Giants’ run against Dreyer stood up as the only run of the day until Tommy Edman emerged from a 2-for-41 slump to hit a solo home run in the sixth inning.
The Dodgers broke the 1-1 tie in the seventh on singles by Max Muncy and Josue De Paula followed by an RBI double from Kiké Hernandez.
They stranded De Paula and Hernandez in scoring position, but singles by Teoscar Hernandez, Freddie Freeman and Muncy produced another run in the eighth inning.
Kris Bubic, Brock Stewart and Tanner Scott combined on 2⅔ innings of hitless relief to close out the combined two-hitter for the Dodgers’ 96th win. With the win, the Dodgers’ magic number to clinch a first-round bye over the Atlanta Braves (who clinched the National League East division title on Sunday) dropped to three with six games left in the regular season.
The Dodgers (96-60) remain two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers (98-58) for the top seed, though the Brewers also hold the head-to-head tiebreaker. The No. 3 seed – currently Atlanta (92-64) – will play host to a best-of-three Wild Card Series against either the Chicago Cubs (87-69), San Diego Padres (87-69) or Philadelphia Phillies (86-70).

item.content:encoded:
Redacción FOX Deportes
Gran noticia para los Dodgers: Shohei Ohtani podría volver pronto
La recuperación del japonés va por buen camino y está por salir de la lista de lesionados
El regreso de Shohei Ohtani a la parte alta del orden al bat de Los Angeles Dodgers parece estar cada vez más cerca. Tras completar otro día favorable en su rutina de bateo, el estelar pelotero se mantiene firme en su camino para salir de la lista de lesionados. Dave Roberts, manager del equipo angelino, confirmó la alta probabilidad de verlo activo durante la próxima serie frente a los San Diego Padres.
La molestia en el bíceps derecho y la rodilla izquierda obligó a aumentar su descanso de quince días. La directiva confía en tenerlo de vuelta este miércoles, justo en el segundo juego de la serie como locales. Sin embargo, su retorno será exclusivo como bateador designado, manteniendo pausada su labor sobre la loma de los disparos.
Su proceso de recuperación dio un salto de calidad tras enfrentar los lanzamientos simulados de la máquina Trajekt. El propio estratega aseguró que el japonés se sintió bastante cómodo luego de tomar entre treinta y cuarenta turnos. Complementando el trabajo físico, el jugador también realizó corridas de bases mientras sus compañeros entrenaban.
El optimismo reina en la plantilla tras la holgada victoria de diez carreras a cuatro frente a San Francisco Giants. La afición angelina ya aguarda con ansias el choque del martes ante San Diego para reencontrarse con su estrella. El bat del fenómeno japonés promete encender la recta final de la temporada regular.

item.title: [New York Post] Dodgers considering Emmet Sheehan for playoff role after gem in win over Giants
item.dc:creator: Dylan Hernandez
item.description: Emmet Sheehan’s next start will be in the minor leagues. The right-hander might be out of sight, but that doesn’t mean he will be out of mind. His scheduled start Saturday for triple-A Oklahoma City in a Pacific Coast League playoff game is part of a design to prepare him to pitch for the Dodgers in October. Sheehan has pitched his way into consideration for a spot on the playoff roster. His quote-unquote demotion came after he pitched 5 ⅓ scoreless innings in the Los Angeles Dodgers’ sweep-seal
item.content:encoded:
Emmet Sheehan’s next start will be in the minor leagues.
The right-hander might be out of sight, but that doesn’t mean he will be out of mind.
His scheduled start Saturday for triple-A Oklahoma City in a Pacific Coast League playoff game is part of a design to prepare him to pitch for the Dodgers in October.
Sheehan has pitched his way into consideration for a spot on the playoff roster.
His quote-unquote demotion came after he pitched 5 ⅓ scoreless innings in the Los Angeles Dodgers’ sweep-sealing 3–1 victory over the San Francisco Giants Sunday.
The game was the third Sheehan pitched this month for the Dodgers. His numbers in those three games: 17 innings pitched, one run allowed, 24 strikeouts, three walks.
“I’ve loved the version we’ve seen of Emmet the last three outings,” manager Dave Roberts said. “He’s been fantastic.”
Sent down to Oklahoma City in early August, Sheehan returned to the major leagues earlier this month with a slightly modified arsenal that has significantly improved his results. He’s thrown his curveball more, and his increased inability to change speeds has made his fastball play up even when he’s not touching 97 mph with it.
“I think that obviously there’s a 97 that plays better, but 94–95 commanded still misses bats,” Roberts said. “So I think that’s something that, that’s one part of it. The other part of it is holding the velocity. And so, for me, the last three or four since he’s been back here, he’s held those 94s and 95s for the, call it, 85 pitches.”
With the Dodgers expecting to start Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell, Tarik Skubal and Tyler Glasnow in the postseason, the team has started the process of moving Sheehan into a relief role by having Jack Dreyer pitch an inning as opener Sunday. Sheehan was down in triple-A over the last week but a roster spot for him was opened up because Skubal went on the bereavement list.
Sheehan entered the game in the second inning and pitched into the seventh. He gave up only one hit and one walk; he struck out nine.
He said he has made it a point to feel “free and easy” with his delivery.
“Instead of saying, ‘I need 97 [mph] here,’ it’s more like, ‘If I hit my spot, he’s not going to hit it,’” Sheehan said.
What it means
The teams with the two-best records in each league will earn a first-round bye and the Dodgers are close to wrapping up one of those spots. With their win over the Giants, the Dodgers maintained a four-game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the National League’s No. 2 seed. Both teams have only six games remaining in the regular season.
Who’s hot
Left-hander Kris Bubic, who was acquired from the Kansas City Royals at the trade deadline, replaced Sheehan in the seventh inning and registered the final two outs of the inning. Bubic struck out Scott Bandura, only for Shay Whitcomb to reach base on a throwing error by Max Muncy.
No problem: Bubic forced Grant McCray to fly out to left field.
Bubic has pitched 2 ⅔ innings in three appearances for the Dodgers over the last week, and he still hasn’t allowed a run. He has struck out four.
Roberts said he’s also pitched his way into consideration for a spot on the playoff roster.
“It’s nothing overpowering, but there’s just funky swings, soft contact,” Roberts said. “I see him as a neutral pitcher, gets left and right out, and I like those converted starters because he knows how to navigate lineups.”
Who’s Not
For today, this section should be renamed “Who Wasn’t Hot.”
The label certainly applied to Tommy Edman, who was two for his last 42 before his sixth-inning at-bat: That’s when Edman jumped on an inside cutter from Carson Seymour and launched it into the visiting bullpen behind the right-field wall.
Edman’s home run tied the game at 1–1.
Up next
The Dodgers have a day off Monday. They will resume play Tuesday when they host the San Diego Padres, who will send No. 1 starter Michael King (12-9, 3.03 ERA) to the mound. The Dodgers won’t have a traditional starter, as Roberts said the team is planning for a bullpen game.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Josue De Paula Breaks Down Viral Clip With Shohei Ohtani
item.dc:creator: Aaron Coloma
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers top prospect Josue De Paula went viral Friday after doing a double take following a high five with Shohei Ohtani. De Paula, who came up to replace Ohtani upon the MVP’s move to the injured list, had a huge game from the No. 9 spot on Friday, going 2-for-3 with two runs and an RBI. His second run of the game came off of a Mookie Betts homer, and he followed the All-Star through the dugout giving high fives to his teammates. Upon reaching Ohtani in the line, De Paula casually g
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers top prospect Josue De Paula went viral Friday after doing a double take following a high five with Shohei Ohtani.
De Paula, who came up to replace Ohtani upon the MVP’s move to the injured list, had a huge game from the No. 9 spot on Friday, going 2-for-3 with two runs and an RBI. His second run of the game came off of a Mookie Betts homer, and he followed the All-Star through the dugout giving high fives to his teammates.
Upon reaching Ohtani in the line, De Paula casually gave him a high five before doing a double take with a surprised look on his face.
“I actually seen him earlier that day but I wasn’t expecting him to be at the game,” De Paula said to Dodgers Nation’s Noel Sanchez. “He caught me by surprise, I was giving everybody a handshake, I gave him a handshake, but then I double take like he’s here.
“I can’t wait until he’s back. To see what he does in the box, you don’t see that every day so I can’t wait.”
De Paula is just 21 years old, and is already making quite the impact with the Dodgers. Through nine games with the team so far, De Paula has a .929 OPS with one homer and seven RBIs. His underlying numbers look great across the board, as he strikes out at an extremely low clip while maintaining fantastic quality of contact in his small MLB sample size.
When Will Shohei Ohtani Be Back?
Ohtani hasn’t played since Sept. 7, as he is nursing a biceps issue. He is slowly returning to baseball activities, and began running the bases prior to Saturday’s game against the San Francisco Giants.
Following Saturday’s game, manager Dave Roberts revealed he could return against the San Diego Padres in the Dodgers’ next series, which begins on Tuesday. His return would be huge for the Dodgers just before the postseason, and while he may not be able to pitch in October, he will play a huge role at the top of the Dodgers’ lineup as they aim to win their third World Series in a row.

But Dodgers manager Dave Roberts appeared to believe that Skubal will be back by Friday, telling reporters he would miss "a
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers placed pitcher Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list on Sunday, which means he could miss his final regular-season turn in the rotation next week.
Skubal's next start is scheduled for Friday against the San Francisco Giants, which could fall within the three-to-seven days that players are allowed to be away from the team while on the bereavement list. But Dodgers manager Dave Roberts appeared to believe that Skubal will be back by Friday, telling reporters he would miss "a couple days."
"Some personal stuff going on, but he's fine," Roberts said, via MLB.com's Sonja Chen.
Skubal pitched in Saturday's 10-4 win over the Giants, allowing four runs and eight hits over five innings. He walked two batters with three strikeouts, tying his lowest total of the season. Saturday's game was the first time Skubal gave up more than three runs in his nine starts with the Dodgers. according to The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya.
Tarik Skubal pitched five innings and allowed four runs but is grateful for the offensive support.
“Yeah, no doubt. Obviously, I wasn't very good today, but the offense and defense and bullpen picked me up big time, and that's what good teams do,” Skubal said. “You know, they… pic.twitter.com/4TUdrQqgH8
"Obviously, I wasn't very good today, but the offense and defense and bullpen picked me up big time, and that's what good teams do," Skubal said after the game.
In his nine starts with the Dodgers since being acquired from the Detroit Tigers before the MLB trade deadline, Skubal has a 2.95 ERA and 4-2 record with 60 strikeouts in 55 innings.
The Dodgers took a 2-0 lead on a first-inning RBI double by Max Muncy and Mookie Betts hitting a run-scoring single in the second. But San Francisco tied the score in the third on a 2-run homer from Victor Bericoto, hitting a fastball left in the very middle of the strike zone by Skubal.
The two teams then traded runs during the third through fifth innings, resulting in a 4-4 tie, before the Dodgers pulled away on a 2-run hit by Tommy Edman and RBI single from Miguel Rojas. In the following inning, the Dodgers added three more runs with Will Smith driving in a run and Josue De Paula hitting a 2-run single.
To fill Skubal's spot on the active roster, Emmet Sheehan was recalled from Triple-A Oklahoma City. He pitched 5 1/3 scoreless innings with one hit allowed and nine strikeouts, taking over for opener Jack Dreyer in the Dodgers' 3-1 win. In his previous two starts before being optioned, Sheehan allowed one run over 11 2/3 innings with 15 strikeouts.

The Dodgers begin their final regular season home series of the year, hosting the San Diego Padres beginning Tuesday night at Dodger Stadium.
Center fielder Andy Pages will likely be activated to start on Tuesday, after missing 27 games with a broken left hand.
It'll be a bullpen game for the Dodgers in the opener, who will start Yoshinobu Yamamoto on Wednesday and likely Tyler Glasnow on Thursday. Roki Sasaki is expected to be available out of the bullpen against the Padres, not as a bulk reliever, but will instead pitch in high-leverage relief, potentially for multiple innings on occasion.
"I trust him," manager Dave Roberts said of Sasaki in relief on Sunday.
Right-hander Michael King starts on the mound for the Padres on Tuesday.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Kiké Hernández hit a go-ahead RBI double in the seventh inning, Emmet Sheehan did not give up a run in 5 1/3 innings, and the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants 3-1 on Sunday to complete a three-game sweep.
Hernández jumped on the first pitch he saw from Sam Hentges (1-7), driving in Max Muncy to put the Dodgers ahead 2-1. Muncy pushed an insurance run across with a single in the eighth.
Kris Bubic (4-2) pitched 2/3 of an inning for the win, and Tanner Scott handled the ninth inning for his 23rd save.
Sheehan made the most of a bullpen game to strengthen his credentials for making the Dodgers’ postseason roster as a long reliever. He had nine strikeouts against one hit and one walk after taking over from Jack Dreyer in the second inning.
Matt Wilkinson allowed three hits and no walks while striking out six in five scoreless innings, but the Giants’ bullpen buckled. The 23-year-old left-hander was acquired as part of the trade that sent catcher Patrick Bailey to Cleveland in May.
Tommy Edman homered to right in the sixth inning to tie the game at 1, tagging reliever Carson Seymour for the 400-foot shot.
Jonah Cox drew a leadoff walk to help spot the Giants their 1-0 lead. Cox reached second on a bad pickoff attempt by Dreyer before stealing third, and Victor Bericoto’s single drove him home.
Up next
Giants: RHP Blade Tidwell (1-2, 4.56 ERA) starts in the opener of a three-game series against the Minnesota Twins on Monday night, facing RHP Bailey Ober (7-6, 4.32).
Dodgers: Manager Dave Roberts said there would be another bullpen game Tuesday night to start a three-game series against the San Diego Padres, who have yet to set their rotation.

Manager Dave Roberts said Ohtani 30 to 40 swings off the Trajekt machine, building on previously hitting against a coach pitching to him on Friday. After the at-bats, Ohtani took the field to run the bases with Dodgers strength coach Travis Smith overseeing the work. Roberts said there now is a “good chance” Ohtani retu
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are counting on Shohei Ohtani returning in time for the start of the playoffs, and Saturday represented his biggest progress toward making that a reality.
Manager Dave Roberts said Ohtani 30 to 40 swings off the Trajekt machine, building on previously hitting against a coach pitching to him on Friday.
After the at-bats, Ohtani took the field to run the bases with Dodgers strength coach Travis Smith overseeing the work. Roberts said there now is a “good chance” Ohtani returns during the upcoming series against the San Diego Padres.
Ohtani is looking to overcome left knee and right arm/bicep trouble that shut him down from being a two-way player and threw his 2026 season well off course.
Although the Dodgers continued to assert otherwise, Ohtani long appeared compromised at the plate because of his lingering injuries. Both the knee and bicep were said to only affect him while pitching.
Ohtani was put on the 15-day injured list with an official designation of right biceps inflammation. He was initially shut down from baseball activities for a few days before beginning the buildup process.
“Everything I’ve heard, it’s been a really productive last three to four to five days. He’s in a good spot,” Roberts said on Friday.
When is Shohei Ohtani returning?
Ohtani is eligible to be activated off the injured list on Sept. 23. Should he return that date, it would amount to having five regular season games to prepare for the playoffs. Ohtani also is going to be activated without first going on a rehab assignment.
Roberts has downplayed any concern over there not being enough time for Ohtani to log a sufficient number of at-bats before the Dodgers begin playing October baseball, which they hope will be with the National League Division Series.
“I think no matter what I say, it really doesn’t matter in the sense of it’s what he feels good with, what gets him ready,” Roberts noted. “So I could say 10, but it could be 12. I think for me, if I’m just kind of spitballing, I think 10 to 12 would be great.”
Whenever Ohtani does return it will be limited to a DH role as the Dodgers all but completely ruled out pitching again this year.

item.title: [Dodger Blue] Mookie Betts makes bold statement about recent success
item.dc:creator: Matt Borelli
item.description: Mookie Betts continued his torrid stretch at the plate in the Los Angeles Dodgers’ 10-4 win over the San Francisco Giants on Saturday night, going 4-for-4 with three doubles, two RBI and a walk. item.content:encoded:
Mookie Betts continued his torrid stretch at the plate in the Los Angeles Dodgers’ 10-4 win over the San Francisco Giants on Saturday night, going 4-for-4 with three doubles, two RBI and a walk.
The big performance came after Betts hit two home runs in Friday’s series opener at Dodger Stadium as part of a 3-for-4 effort at the plate. He is now 10-for-12 with five extra-base hits, five RBI, five runs scored and three walks over his last three games.
“Yeah, I mean, this is it,” Betts said when asked if this is the version of himself that he has been chasing. “I know I’m still capable of it; it’s in there somewhere. So just got to keep on rolling, keep on, like I said, laying the foundation and letting the game be the game.”
Betts has been one of the Dodgers’ hottest hitters over the past month after struggling offensively for much of the season. He is hitting a stellar .359/.449/.652 with nine doubles, six home runs and 21 RBI over his last 28 games.
Betts attributed his recent success to seeing the ball better and his swing finally being in a good spot.
“Oh, I think it’s both,” Betts began. “Swing is a little more consistent, hitting balls in the middle of the zone hard, and able to take balls. So that’s the name of the game. Hit strikes hard and take balls.”
Betts has consistently tinkered with his swing this year and is now reaping the rewards of his hard work. His resurgence couldn’t have come at a better time for the Dodgers, who are playing out the final week of the regular season before beginning what they hope will be a deep playoff run.
Dave Roberts surprised by Mookie Betts
Roberts has stood by Betts all season, but even he didn’t expect the eight-time All-Star to bounce back in such a big way.
“You know, I didn’t,” Roberts admitted. “I couldn’t tell you that I saw this, but I just felt that he was stronger. He’s worked hard on that. He looks great. He’s not going to stop working, and just for it to come together has been great.
“I think for me, it’s just trying to keep him confident. His teammates have poured into him, and again, it’s as good as we’ve seen him over a consistent period in a while.”

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Is it still a rivalry? Dodgers complete sweep of woeful Giants
item.dc:creator: Kevin Baxter
item.description: Is it still a rivalry? Dodgers complete sweep of woeful Giants - Click here to listen to this article - Only the Pirates and Cubs have met more often than the Dodgers and Giants, who faced off for the first time in 1889. item.content:encoded:
Is it still a rivalry? Dodgers complete sweep of woeful Giants
- Click here to listen to this article
-
Only the Pirates and Cubs have met more often than the Dodgers and Giants, who faced off for the first time in 1889. And over all that time, the Dodgers are just two games better, with 1,294 wins to the Giants’ 1,292.
The Dodgers and Giants have also won more pennants, made more World Series appearances and have more players wearing their caps in the Hall of Fame than any other National League teams, all of which fueled a rivalry that was once among the most visceral and passionate in American sports.
But that was then and this is now.
After Sunday’s 3-1 victory over the Giants, the Dodgers’ 14th win in their last 17 games, the team could finish a season with 100 wins for the fourth time in six years. The Giants have had just one winning record in that time.
The Dodgers (96-60), who have won five straight division titles, are headed to the postseason for a record-tying 14th consecutive year. The Giants will miss the playoffs for a fifth straight season.
So is the rivalry dead? That depends on who you ask.
“It’s always a rivalry,” Giants pitcher Logan Webb. “We’d like to make it a little closer when it comes to the standings. But I definitely feel it when I throw against them.”
But then Webb, who is from Northern California, grew up with the rivalry and, as the longest-tenured Giant, pitched against the Dodgers in games that mattered. Giants coach Ron Washington, who made his major league debut with the Dodgers when the rivalry was still a thing, said many players on San Francisco’s roster don’t know that background.
Mookie Betts hits three doubles and the Dodgers piled up 15 hits in a 10-4 win over the San Francisco Giants with Shohei Ohtani’s return on the horizon.
“It should be a rivalry. But I don’t think the young kids we got know anything about a rivalry. They’re not history buffs.”
Webb said it’s the responsibility of the veterans on both sides to keep that history alive by explaining the enmity to the young players.
“I think there are still guys that came up in the system that know what it’s like,” he said. “It’s my job to kind of hype these guys up to play a game like this.”
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts, who played for the Dodgers and Giants during his 10-year career, agrees the rivalry now exists more in the history books than the current standings, where the Giants have been overtaken by the San Diego Padres, who will finish second to the Dodgers in the N.L. West for the fourth time in five seasons.
“It’s certainly a rivalry in the sense of the history, the fan bases,” Roberts said. “But obviously it’s about relevancy. The Padres have been successful the last handful of years, and so it’s certainly built some momentum. The geography lends itself to that too.
“But Dodgers Giants is always fun.”
It hasn’t been so much fun for the Giants lately. San Francisco hasn’t won the season series with the Dodgers since 2021 and has lost more than 90 games this year for the first time in nine seasons.
On Sunday they went in front three batters into the game with Johan Cox working Dodger opener Jack Dreyer for a leadoff walk, then making his way around the bases on Dreyer’s throwing error, a stolen base and a one-one single by Victor Bericoto.
But San Francisco didn’t get another hit until Jung Hoo Lee singled with one out in the sixth.
That allowed the Dodgers to tie the score in the sixth on Tommy Edman’s seventh home run of the season just inside the right-field foul pole. An inning later they went ahead to stay when Max Muncy singled under a sliding Cox at second, moved to third on a single by rookie Josue De Paula and scored on Kiké Hernández’s double to center.
A two-out single by Muncy, his second of the game, scored Teoscar Hernández, who also had two hits, in the eighth inning with the final run.
Even the slumping Freddie Freeman contributed to the Dodgers’ 11-hit attack, ending an 0-for-11 slide with a broken-bat single in the fourth then singling again in the eighth.
Sunday’s result helped clarify the Dodgers’ once-muddy playoff picture. With six games left in the regular season, the Dodgers lead Atlanta by four games in the race for the second seed in the National League playoffs, which would give them a first-round bye and the homefield advantage in the division series.
The team’s postseason roster may be getting clearer as well. Right-hander Emmet Sheehan, who made 22 starts this season, came out of the bullpen for the first time Sunday and was brilliant in his audition for the playoffs.
“If there is a role in the postseason, it will be out of the [bull]pen,” Roberts said of Sheehan, who gave up just a hit and walk, striking out nine — one off his season high — in 5 1/3 innings.
Tyler Glasnow hasn’t had the greatest of seasons, but the Dodgers will need him to deliver in the playoffs if they want to win another World Series title.
De Paula, meanwhile, who also doubled in running his modest hitting streak to four games, appears to have secured a job as the team’s left-handed bat off the bench while utility player Hyeseong Kim, who has spent the last four months in the minors, will rejoin the Dodgers after the triple-A playoffs and be considered for a roster spot as a pinch-runner and late-inning defensive replacement.
“My expectation is that Hyeseong will be here during the off week and potentially be a conversation for the postseason because he has the ability to run, play defense, and steal a base,” Roberts said.
After Monday’s off day, the final break of the regular season for the Dodgers, the team is expected to activate Andy Pages, Roki Sasaki and Shohei Ohtani from the injured list during its three-game series with the Padres.

item.title: [presstelegram.com] Dodgers’ Dave Roberts trying to find ‘balance’ as Freddie Freeman struggles to rediscover his swing
item.dc:creator: Bill Plunkett
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Dave Roberts has a dilemma. His first baseman, Freddie Freeman, just turned 37 years old and has been slumping badly down the stretch while playing through patellar tendinitis in his right knee. Never one to accept days off as the answer to anything, Freeman would probably benefit from some downtime this week – but he also needs at-bats to rediscover the swing that had him batting .300 for the season just two weeks ago or recalibrate it to accommodate his balky knee. “There’s rest,
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Dave Roberts has a dilemma.
His first baseman, Freddie Freeman, just turned 37 years old and has been slumping badly down the stretch while playing through patellar tendinitis in his right knee. Never one to accept days off as the answer to anything, Freeman would probably benefit from some downtime this week – but he also needs at-bats to rediscover the swing that had him batting .300 for the season just two weeks ago or recalibrate it to accommodate his balky knee.
“There’s rest, but there’s also trying to find your swing,” Roberts acknowledged after putting Freeman in the lineup on Saturday and Sunday – a day game following a night game.
“I think it’s a work in progress,” Roberts said of Freeman’s swing. “The other day in Cincinnati (a three-hit game on Tuesday), I think it was looking pretty good, and then. I actually thought yesterday there were a couple good swings there.
“Obviously, the results weren’t there for him, and he’s frustrated, and I think that you just kind of have to count on him to figure it out and bet on him. And that’s kind of where we’re at. But again, having the week off (with a first-round bye) would be huge too.”
Freeman said he has been doing some different drills in the batting cage, focused on hitting the ball “out front” more.
“I feel like my faults are I try to hit the ball to the opposite field too much, and I let the ball get too deep, and it caused me to slide,” Freeman said earlier this week. “So today (in the cage) was – foot down early, catch the ball out front a little bit.”
Even with that three-hit game in Cincinnati and a two-hit game on Thursday, Freeman went into Sunday just 6 for his past 48 (.125), hitless in nine at-bats in the first two games of the series with the Giants.
“Got to go for results-based things right now,” Freeman said. “Looking to be hot for a few weeks. That’s all I’m trying to do.
“I’m just trying to find something that gives me results. We’re at the time where we’re just trying to get hot for five weeks here. So kind of like I did in the World Series a couple years ago (when his ankle was injured), I did the step-out move. That’s not sustainable over six months. I’m not trying to find something that’s sustainable. I’m trying to find something that works for four weeks.”
OHTANI WORK
The “hope” is that Shohei Ohtani will be ready to come off the injured list when he is eligible on Wednesday, Roberts said. When he does, Roberts expects him to be in the lineup for the final five games.
“Absolutely,” Roberts said. “Yeah, he’ll need those live at-bats.”
Roberts has said Ohtani is “pain-free” but he acknowledged that Ohtani won’t be feeling 100% when he returns – but will be closer to it than he has been in weeks.
“Discomfort you can play through,” Roberts said of how Ohtani is feeling. “I think there’s a difference between discomfort and pain. Is it 100%? Probably not. Is it better than it was a week ago? Yes.
“Honestly I think that’s just a better question for Shohei to give more specifics, but I do think that when he’s activated it’s going to be the best physical place he’s been in in quite some time.”
Ohtani has spoken with the media just once in the past five weeks (before he went on the IL).
KIM CALL
Signed to a three-year, $12.5 million contract, South Korean infielder Hyeseong Kim has spent most of the second season of that contract in Triple-A where he hit .265 with a .682 OPS in 84 games. He hasn’t been up with the Dodgers since May but Roberts said Kim will be part of the “conversation” for the postseason roster.
“My expectation is Hyeseong will be here during the off week (next week) and potentially be a conversation for the postseason (roster) because he has the ability to run, to play defense, and steal a base,” Roberts said. “He’s in the conversation, yes.”
Kim was on the postseason roster last fall, appearing in just two games. It will be difficult to give him a spot on a bench that seems set with Alex Call, Hunter Feduccia, Miguel Rojas, Kiké Hernandez and Josue De Paula.
ROSTER MOVES
The Dodgers placed pitcher Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list on Sunday and recalled Emmet Sheehan from Triple-A to pitch ‘bulk’ in Sunday’s game.
Also, reliever Seth Halvorsen was returned to Triple-A and reliever Kyle Hurt was recalled.
Sheehan is still under consideration for a bullpen role on the postseason roster.
UP NEXT
The Dodgers are off on Monday.
Padres (TBA) at Dodgers (TBA), Tuesday, 7:10 p.m., SportsNet LA, 570 AM

item.title: [MLB.com] How Sheehan, Sasaki and others look to fit in LA's postseason 'pen plans
item.dc:creator: Sonja Chen
item.description: LOS ANGELES -- The saying goes that pitching wins championships, and that was true in different ways when the Dodgers won back-to-back World Series in 2024 and '25. The 2024 Dodgers had to lean heavily on their bullpen out of necessity, while the '25 team rode its rotation to a successful title defense -- so much so that all four starting pitchers took the ball in the winner-take-all Game 7. As the Dodgers go for a three-peat this year, they'll once again look for their starting four of Yoshinob
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- The saying goes that pitching wins championships, and that was true in different ways when the Dodgers won back-to-back World Series in 2024 and '25.
The 2024 Dodgers had to lean heavily on their bullpen out of necessity, while the '25 team rode its rotation to a successful title defense -- so much so that all four starting pitchers took the ball in the winner-take-all Game 7.
As the Dodgers go for a three-peat this year, they'll once again look for their starting four of Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow to set the tone. But their bullpen feels less volatile than it was last year, and it could be one of the most fluid position groups as L.A. considers how to piece together its postseason rosters.
One way or another, the Dodgers will carry their best 13 pitchers in the postseason, because as manager Dave Roberts has said repeatedly, like a mantra: "Every inning in the postseason is leverage."
The Dodgers got a look at several postseason 'pen candidates when they ran a bullpen game to success on Sunday afternoon at Dodger Stadium, capping a three-game sweep of the Giants with a 3-1 victory. Right-hander Emmet Sheehan struck out nine in 5 1/3 scoreless innings of bulk relief, giving L.A. an intriguing option to add to the mix.
The Dodgers' fourth straight victory maintained their four-game lead over the Braves for the second-best record in the National League -- and a first-round postseason bye -- with six games left to play.
The greatest need in the bullpen is right-handed leverage arms. Edwin Díaz, who signed a three-year, $69 million deal to be their closer, has been relegated to lower leverage for the time being amid his poor performance in an injury-ravaged season. Edgardo Henriquez, who stepped up to become L.A.'s most reliable righty in leverage, is out for the rest of the regular season due to a lower back strain. He could return during the postseason, but the uncertainty still creates a need.
Evan Phillips and Brock Stewart have been solid options, but they have been more valuable as part of the bridge to the ninth inning, rather than to close out games. In order to find such options from the right-hand side, the Dodgers can turn to the strength of their staff: the rotation.
Sheehan is one candidate, although he'll remain stretched out through the end of the regular season as rotation depth. Another is Roki Sasaki, who was also originally going to remain built up as a starter upon his return from the 15-day IL. Instead, Roberts said, Sasaki will likely be activated Tuesday and be available out of the bullpen, beginning his transition to relief in the final days of the regular season.
"He's done it. He's really good. He's a neutral pitcher, high-octane stuff," Roberts said. "You really just need four starters, you know. So we're in a good spot there for now."
Sheehan and Sasaki both got a crash course in short-burst relief last fall. While Sasaki thrived as the Dodgers' postseason closer, Sheehan was scored on in his first four appearances before rebounding for scoreless outings in Games 3 and 7 of the World Series.
For Sheehan, adapting his typical routine to relief was difficult, but he believes that he can build on last year if he gets the call to the 'pen again.
"Having that experience helps a lot," Sheehan said. "Just getting back into that, I know what I need to do to get ready to go into the game."
And don't count out Díaz. His pitch to earn a spot in the postseason 'pen began with two scoreless innings against the Giants this weekend.
When the postseason comes, the Dodgers may not be able to avoid using Díaz in leverage, even if they don't throw him into a comparable situation in the final days of the regular season. But if he shows enough this week, then L.A. will bet on his track record.
"I gotta show them I’m part of that bullpen," Díaz said. "I haven’t pitched [much] this year, and when I’ve been on the mound I’ve been struggling. So right now, I’m giving my 200% just to show them I will be in that roster spot."

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers Manager Makes Surprise Admission About Mookie Betts' Resurgence
item.dc:creator: J P Hoornstra; Unknown
