Betts looks immovable right now, especially on the heels of a game in which he reached base five times. He collected three doubles, a single and a walk in the Dodgers' 10-4 win on Saturday at Dodger Stadium. Betts' September surge marks an abrupt change from the five months that came before. Through the end of August, Betts' .701 OPS ranked 12
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers shortstop Mookie Betts led off in manager Dave Roberts' lineup for the third consecutive game Sunday against the San Francisco Giants. Betts looks immovable right now, especially on the heels of a game in which he reached base five times. He collected three doubles, a single and a walk in the Dodgers' 10-4 win on Saturday at Dodger Stadium.
Betts' September surge marks an abrupt change from the five months that came before.
Through the end of August, Betts' .701 OPS ranked 123rd out of 163 major league hitters with at least 400 plate appearances. Since Sept. 1, his OPS was an outstanding 1.287 entering Sunday, trailing only Cincinnati Reds shortstop Elly De La Cruz among 181 qualified hitters this month.
"I couldn’t tell you that I saw this,” Roberts said Saturday, referring to Betts' dramatic turnaround. “But I just felt that he was stronger. He’s worked hard on that. He looks great. He’s not going to stop working, and just for it to come together has been great.”
The Dodgers will have a choice to make if and when Shohei Ohtani returns from the injured list. Ostensibly he'll go back to the leadoff spot again, though his health — and Betts' resurgence — are at least making it a conversation.
For the Dodgers, it's a good problem to have at the right time.
At 33, Betts is facing many of the same questions the Dodgers' other 30-and-over stars face anytime their performance slips. Has age caught up to them? Can they maintain their performance through the end of October? Do the Dodgers need a younger player to take their place in order to repeat as World Series champions?
The questions apply to Miguel Rojas (37), Freddie Freeman (36), Max Muncy (35), Kiké Hernández (34), Teoscar Hernández (33), Tommy Edman (31) and Ohtani (31), as well as Betts.
Professional athletes are famously the last to know when their physical skills are no longer enough to justify their roster spot. Take it with a grain of salt, but Betts isn't worried about his ability to maintain his current stretch of play.
“I mean this is it,” Betts said of his recent form. “I know I’m still capable of it, it’s in there somewhere. So, just gotta keep on rolling, keep on laying the foundation and letting the game be the game.”
Sign up for our free newsletter and follow us on X/Twitter and Facebook for the latest news.
J.P. Hoornstra is an On SI Contributor. A veteran of 20 years of sports coverage for daily newspapers in California, J.P. covered MLB, the Los Angeles Dodgers, and the Los Angeles Angels (occasionally of Anaheim) from 2012-23 for the Southern California News Group. His first book, The 50 Greatest Dodgers Games of All-Time, published in 2015. In 2016, he won an Associated Press Sports Editors award for breaking news coverage. He once recorded a keyboard solo on the same album as two of the original Doors.

item.description: Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles llamaron de vuelta al lanzador Emmet Sheehan como parte de una serie de movimientos en el roster el domingo, y está previsto que el derecho se encargue de la mayor parte del juego en el cierre de la serie contra los Gigantes de San Francisco. Las cuatro transacciones involucraron a lanzadores de los Dodgers. También llamaron de vuelta a Kyle Hurt, colocaron a Tarik Skubal en la lista de duelo y enviaron a Seth Halvorsen a Triple-A Oklahoma City. Movimientos en el roste
item.content:encoded:
Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles llamaron de vuelta al lanzador Emmet Sheehan como parte de una serie de movimientos en el roster el domingo, y está previsto que el derecho se encargue de la mayor parte del juego en el cierre de la serie contra los Gigantes de San Francisco.
Las cuatro transacciones involucraron a lanzadores de los Dodgers. También llamaron de vuelta a Kyle Hurt, colocaron a Tarik Skubal en la lista de duelo y enviaron a Seth Halvorsen a Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Movimientos en el roster de los Dodgers
Jack Dreyer abrirá mientras los Dodgers buscan la barrida ante sus rivales del Área de la Bahía, antes de cederle el turno a Sheehan.
"Hoy estamos armando esto un poco con las opciones disponibles. Creo que se trata más de lo que, en nuestra opinión, le da a Emmet la mejor oportunidad", comentó el mánager Dave Roberts.
El jardinero derecho Kyle Tucker no estará en la alineación después de salir de la victoria del sábado por 10-4 debido a un lanzamiento foul que le pegó en la rodilla derecha.
Lesiones y esperanzas de regreso
Los Dodgers esperan ver pronto de regreso a Shohei Ohtani tras su primera estancia en la lista de lesionados desde que se unió al equipo en 2024. Podría ocurrir durante una serie de tres juegos contra los San Diego Padres que comienza la noche del martes. "Aún está en el aire, pero esa es nuestra esperanza", señaló Roberts.
Ohtani está en la lista de lesionados de 15 días por una inflamación en el bíceps derecho. También ha estado lidiando con molestias en la rodilla izquierda desde hace meses.
Expectativas sobre el regreso de Ohtani
Roberts cree que Ohtani llegará sin dolor a la última semana de la temporada regular, mientras los Dodgers presionan para asegurar un descanso y evitar la ronda de comodines.
"Creo que hay una diferencia entre molestia y dolor. ¿Está al 100 por ciento? Probablemente no. ¿Está mejor que hace una semana? Sí", manifestó Roberts.

item.title: [FOX Sports] Dodgers Star Shohei Ohtani Could Return To Lineup On Wednesday Against Padres
item.description: Dodgers Star Shohei Ohtani Could Return To Lineup On Wednesday Against Padres Shohei Ohtani could make his return for the Los Angeles Dodgers sooner rather than later. Speaking to reporters on Sunday, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts provided an encouraging update on Ohtani, revealing that he could return as early as Wednesday and is expected to play every game down the stretch once activated. Roberts also believes it’s important for Ohtani to get as many at-bats as possible once he returns to the f
item.content:encoded:
Dodgers Star Shohei Ohtani Could Return To Lineup On Wednesday Against Padres
Shohei Ohtani could make his return for the Los Angeles Dodgers sooner rather than later.
Speaking to reporters on Sunday, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts provided an encouraging update on Ohtani, revealing that he could return as early as Wednesday and is expected to play every game down the stretch once activated.
Roberts also believes it’s important for Ohtani to get as many at-bats as possible once he returns to the field.
Through 130 games, Ohtani is batting .277 with 30 home runs, 80 RBIs, and a .902 OPS. While his offensive numbers rank among the league's elite, Ohtani won't return to the mound this season or during the playoffs as he focuses exclusively on hitting.
Regardless of his status on the mound, the plan remains to maximize Ohtani’s impact at the plate as much as possible. The Dodgers continue to hold firm control of the National League West with a 95-60 record and a nine-game lead in first place.
If Ohtani can return on Wednesday against the San Diego Padres, it will mark his first game back since Sept. 7. For a Dodgers team eyeing a historic three-peat, inserting Ohtani’s bat back into the lineup provides a massive boost heading into the postseason.

The Los Angeles Dodgers are currently taking on the San Francisco Giants in a weekend series.
With the NL West already wrapped up, the Dodgers are just a few wins away from locking up the No. 2 seed in the NL.
Before the Giants game on Sunday, LA announced its starter, with the anticipation that the contest would be a bullpen game.
Jack Dreyer Gets Start As Opener on Sunday
On Sunday, reliever Jack Dreyer will get the start against the Giants.
@UnderdogMLB revealed the news:
Dodgers: "9/20 M. Betts SS T. Edman CF T. Hernández RF F. Freeman 1B M. Rojas 2B M. Muncy 3B J. De Paula DH E. Hernández LF H. Feduccia C J. Dreyer SP"
Hunter Feduccia is doing the catching duties on Sunday afternoon.
@FabianArdaya wrote:
"Jack Dreyer is opening today. Emmet Sheehan has a locker. So does Kyle Hurt."
So, sounds like there could be some roster moves before Sunday's contest as well.
Taking a Quick Look at Jack Dreyer
Jack Dreyer has been a very solid reliever for the Dodgers over the past two seasons.
In 59.1 innings pitched with LA in 2026, Dreyer carries an ERA of 3.19 with 68 strikeouts.
Dreyer has logged 135.2 IP in his MLB career, and over that span, he holds an ERA of 3.05 with 142 Ks, a WHIP of 1.084, and a pitching record of 8-4.
It will be interesting to see how Dreyer can aid the Dodgers on Sunday, and how Dave Roberts handles the bullpen in the bulk outing.

item.title: [truebluela.com] Dodgers call up Emmet Sheehan, with Tarik Skubal on bereavement leave
item.dc:creator: Eric Stephen
item.description: LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers made a number of pitching moves ahead of Sunday’s series finale against the San Francisco Giants. Tarik Skubal, who started on Saturday, was placed on bereavement leave, which facilitated the return of Emmet Sheehan from Triple-A Oklahoma City. In addition, reliever Kyle Hurt was recalled and Seth Halvorsen optioned in a swap of right-handers in the bullpen. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers made a number of pitching moves ahead of Sunday’s series finale against the San Francisco Giants. Tarik Skubal, who started on Saturday, was placed on bereavement leave, which facilitated the return of Emmet Sheehan from Triple-A Oklahoma City. In addition, reliever Kyle Hurt was recalled and Seth Halvorsen optioned in a swap of right-handers in the bullpen.
Sheehan was just optioned on Monday and normally would have needed to stay in the minors for 15 days, but because he’s replacing a player on the bereavement list (or injured list or paternity list) that allows the right-hander to return early.
After getting sent down to Triple-A on August 3, Sheehan turned his season around, including winning Pacific Coast League pitcher of the month, and he allowed one run in 11 2/3 innings last week for the Dodgers before getting optioned to Oklahoma City so the Dodgers could use a fresh arm. In his last five outings — three in Triple-A, two with Dodgers — Sheehan has allowed only two runs in 29 innings with 39 strikeouts (36.4-percent strikeout rate) against only eight walks.
All 26 outings by Sheehan this season have been starts, but on Sunday he’ll follow an opener in left-hander Jack Dreyer. Sunday provides at least a practice run of Sheehan’s most likely role in the postseason, pitching in bulk relief.
“Emmet’s a part of the conversation,” manager Dave Roberts said Sunday, “but if there is a role in the postseason it would be out of the ’pen.”
Bereavement leave lasts for a minimum of three days and up to seven, so Skubal wouldn’t be activated until Wednesday at the earliest. But considering the left-hander just started on Saturday, don’t expect him to be activated until his start day, likely next weekend in San Francisco.
Halvorsen has allowed nine runs in 10 innings with the Dodgers, including three home runs, with six strikeouts and two walks. He pitched a scoreless inning on Saturday, which was his third appearance in four days.
Hurt pitched a scoreless inning for Oklahoma City on Friday, his only appearance in the last week. Since getting optioned on September 5, Hurt pitched in three games for Oklahoma City, all scoreless innings. This season with the Dodgers, Hurt has a 4.33 ERA and 3.84 xERA in 43 games, with 56 strikeouts and 23 walks in 43 2/3 innings.
Saturday was his 15th day on optional assignment in Triple-A, making Sunday his first day eligible to return from the minors.

item.dc:creator: DAN GREENSPAN

All four transactions involved Dodgers pitchers. They also recalled Kyle Hurt, placed Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list and optioned Seth Halvorsen to Triple-A Oklahoma City. Jack Dreyer will start as the Dodgers go for the sweep against their Bay Area rivals before giving way
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — The Los Angeles Dodgers recalled pitcher Emmet Sheehan as part of a series of roster moves Sunday, with the right-hander set to handle the bulk of their series finale against the San Francisco Giants.
All four transactions involved Dodgers pitchers. They also recalled Kyle Hurt, placed Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list and optioned Seth Halvorsen to Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Jack Dreyer will start as the Dodgers go for the sweep against their Bay Area rivals before giving way to Sheehan, who is 5-8 with a 4.79 ERA in 22 games this season.
“Kind of piecing through the available options today,” manager Dave Roberts said. “I think it's just more of what gives Emmet, in our opinion, the best chance.”
Right fielder Kyle Tucker won't be in the lineup after coming out of Saturday's 10-4 victory because of a fouled pitch that went off his right knee. The early exit was described as precautionary, and Roberts felt it was worth giving him a day off, particularly with Tucker finding his stride after an erratic first season in Los Angeles. He is batting .429 with five homers, eight extra-base hits and 11 RBIs in his past 10 games.
The Dodgers expect to see Shohei Ohtani back soon after his first stint on the injured list since joining the team in 2024. It could come during a three-game series against the San Diego Padres that starts Tuesday night. “Still up in the air, but that’s our hope,” Roberts said.
Ohtani is on the 15-day IL with right biceps inflammation. He also has been dealing with left knee soreness for months.
Roberts believes Ohtani will be pain-free going into the last week of the regular season, with the Dodgers pushing to secure a bye to avoid the wild-card round.
“I think there's a difference between discomfort and pain,” Roberts said. “Is it 100%? Probably not. Is it better than it was a week ago? Yes. Honestly, I think that's just a better question for Shohei to give specifics. But I do think that when he's activated, it's going to be the best physical place he's been in in quite some time.”

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal is going on the bereavement list, manager Dave Roberts announced on Sunday.
The move came a day after Skubal suffered his worst start with the Dodgers, giving up four runs in five innings in Saturday’s 10-4 win over the San Francisco Giants.
In his absence, Emmet Sheehan was called up from triple-A, returning in hopes of building off back-to-back strong starts earlier this month. He will follow opener Jack Dreyer on Sunday as the bulk pitcher for the Dodgers’ series finale with the Giants.
Roberts said Skubal would be away from the Dodgers for “a couple days.” No further information on his situation was available.
Skubal is a contender to be the Dodgers’ Game 1 starter in the playoffs, after being acquired in a blockbuster deal at the trade deadline in August. Even after Saturday’s setback, in which he allowed eight hits and bemoaned his lack of fastball command, the left-hander is 4-2 with a 2.95 ERA in nine starts with the Dodgers this season.
The two-time Cy Young Award winner will anchor a postseason rotation also expected to include Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tyler Glasnow and Blake Snell (assuming he continues to recover from his recent groin injury).
The Dodgers also freshened up their bullpen on Sunday, swapping out right-handers was calling up Kyle Hurt and optioning Seth Halvorsen.
The team enters Sunday with the chance to not only sweep the Giants, but further lower their current magic number of four to secure a first-round bye in the playoffs.
They enter play on Sunday four games ahead of the Atlanta Braves for the No. 2 seed in the National League.

item.content:encoded:
Kyle Tucker has started to heat up at the perfect time for the Los Angeles Dodgers. Signed this past offseason to a massive four-year, $240 million deal, he spent most of the summer struggling at the plate and unable to string together any consistent production. Just when it seemed like he would get hot, he would slide right back into another cold stretch.
However, September has been a different story entirely for Tucker. Over 18 games this month, the 29-year-old has posted a .288 batting average, .397 on-base percentage, 1.075 OPS, six home runs and 13 RBIs, while striking out just seven times and walking 12. The discipline and production have both been at an elite level.
The Dodgers are on the verge of clinching a first-round bye in the National League, and Tucker's surge has undoubtedly been a big reason why.
During Saturday's win against the San Francisco Giants, Tucker fouled a ball off his right shin and appeared to be in some discomfort. He remained in the game and finished it, and manager Dave Roberts said afterward he did not expect it to be an issue moving forward.
However, Tucker was not included in Sunday's series finale lineup against San Francisco. Teoscar Hernandez shifted to right field with Enrique Hernandez taking over the vacated spot in left field.
Speaking with reporters pregame, Tucker continued to downplay the issue and revealed he did not undergo any further testing. "I feel fine," Tucker said, per Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic.
Kyle Tucker: “I feel fine.”
Said he didn’t get any further testing. Like he said yesterday, hit him on a different spot than where he broke his shin in 2024. https://t.co/8KvewI1fkA
Tucker has an injury history with his right shin, previously breaking it back in 2024 when he was with the Houston Astros.
However, this situation is nowhere near as serious, and he will look to return for Tuesday's series opener against the San Diego Padres. It is unclear if he will be available off the bench Sunday.

item.description: LOS ANGELES -- The Dodgers made a flurry of roster moves before Sunday afternoon's series finale against the Giants, placing left-hander Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list, recalling right-handers Emmet Sheehan and Kyle Hurt from Triple-A Oklahoma City and optioning right-hander Seth Halvorsen. The Dodgers also gave right fielder Kyle Tucker Sunday off after he fouled a ball off the lower knee/upper shin area on his right leg on Saturday night. Manager Dave Roberts does not think the soreness
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- The Dodgers made a flurry of roster moves before Sunday afternoon's series finale against the Giants, placing left-hander Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list, recalling right-handers Emmet Sheehan and Kyle Hurt from Triple-A Oklahoma City and optioning right-hander Seth Halvorsen.
The Dodgers also gave right fielder Kyle Tucker Sunday off after he fouled a ball off the lower knee/upper shin area on his right leg on Saturday night. Manager Dave Roberts does not think the soreness will become an ongoing issue for Tucker, who is expected back in the lineup on Tuesday.
Here's how these moves will impact the Dodgers on Sunday and beyond:
Skubal will be away from the team for "a couple days," Roberts said. Players may spend between three to seven days on the bereavement list, so Skubal might not miss his next start, which is projected to come on Friday in San Francisco.
"Some personal stuff going on," Roberts said, "but he's fine."
Skubal is 4-2 with a 2.95 ERA in nine starts since being dealt to L.A. ahead of the Trade Deadline.
Sheehan was set to pitch bulk innings on Sunday behind opener Jack Dreyer. The thought was that pitching Sheehan behind an opener could not only help him get deeper into the game, but also prepare him for a possible bullpen role in the postseason, which would be his only path to making the roster.
In his previous two starts for the Dodgers, Sheehan allowed one earned run across 11 2/3 innings. After a strong stint in Triple-A, he has looked to trend in the right direction in what has been an inconsistent season overall (5-8, 4.79 ERA).
Tucker has heated up at the end of the first season of his four-year, $240 million contract, which has been disappointing (his .728 OPS is on track to be a career-worst mark in a full season). Since Sept. 9, he's hitting 15-for-35 (.429) with five home runs and 35 total bases, his most in a 10-game span this season.
On Saturday, Tucker exited the game after six innings due to a combination of the hit-by-pitch and the lopsided score. He said he feels fine, but Roberts decided to give him an extra day to rest after Tucker had played the previous nine games without a day off.
"I feel like everyone's grinding at this point in the season," Tucker said. "But I'll be good with it."

Seth Halvorsen has also been optioned and Kyle Hurt and Emmet Sheehan are back. Skubal last pitched for the Dodgers on Saturday, and had a frustrating outing—h
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers starter Tarik Skubal moved to the bereavement list on Sunday, and will be there for a "couple of days," per Dave Roberts.
In corresponding moves, the Dodgers optioned Seth Halvorsen and recalled Emmet Sheehan and Kyle Hurt.
BREAKING: Tarik Skubal will be away from the Dodgers for a couple days due to personal reasons ?
Seth Halvorsen has also been optioned and Kyle Hurt and Emmet Sheehan are back.
Skubal last pitched for the Dodgers on Saturday, and had a frustrating outing—his worst since donning a Dodgers uniform. He lasted just five innings, allowing four earned runs on eight hits while recording a season-low three strikeouts.
What Does Tarik Skubal's Absence Mean?
The left-hander's presence on the bereavement list doesn't impact the rest of the Dodgers' season, as he will likely be ready for his next turn through the rotation if he stays out for a couple of days as Roberts said.
That should be a huge relief for the Dodgers, who have quite a few injuries among their starters as the postseason nears. Shohei Ohtani, Roki Sasaki and Eric Lauer are all on the IL, leaving LA with limited options.
An injury or extended period of absence for any of their remaining starters would throw a wrench in their plans for the postseason.
Additionally, Skubal's track record since joining the team is fantastic—serving as one of their best starters since the beginning of August. He has a 2.95 ERA through nine starts, striking out 60 batters through 55 innings pitched.
What Roles Will Kyle Hurt and Emmet Sheehan Play?
Hurt and Sheehan are likely to jump straight into the action, as the Dodgers are running a bullpen game on Sunday.
Jack Dreyer is getting the start, but using Hurt and Sheehan—both of whom have experience handling bulk innings—afterwards is the Dodgers' most likely move.
The duo have bounced between Triple-A and MLB over the past few weeks, but could very well find a spot on the team if they perform well Sunday. Sheehan is in the midst of a fantastic run of form, and has capitalized on both of his MLB opportunities in Setpember.
He only allowed one earned run through 11.2 innings pitched over his last two starts, and is a real candidate to make the postseason roster despite his recent stays in the minors.
Before that, though, he'll have to perform in Sunday's game against the Giants, which begins at 1:10 p.m. PT.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Tarik Skubal Away From Team as Dodgers Call Up Emmet Sheehan in Massive 4-Player Roster Move
item.dc:creator: Noah Camras; Unknown
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers announced a major roster move ahead of Sunday's series finale against the San Francisco Giants. The Dodgers have recalled right-handed pitchers Emmet Sheehan and Kyle Hurt from Triple-A. Sheehan will take down bulk innings on Sunday as LA looks to preserve the bullpen heading into the final week of the regular season. As for the corresponding moves, left-handed pitcher Tarik Skubal was placed on the bereavement list and will be away from the team for "a couple days," per
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers announced a major roster move ahead of Sunday's series finale against the San Francisco Giants.
The Dodgers have recalled right-handed pitchers Emmet Sheehan and Kyle Hurt from Triple-A. Sheehan will take down bulk innings on Sunday as LA looks to preserve the bullpen heading into the final week of the regular season.
As for the corresponding moves, left-handed pitcher Tarik Skubal was placed on the bereavement list and will be away from the team for "a couple days," per manager Dave Roberts. Additionally, right-hander Seth Halvorsen was optioned.
Dodgers Recall Emmet Sheehan, Kyle Hurt
Sheehan was surprisingly demoted this past week amid a dominant stretch of play.
Across his last two starts at the MLB level, Sheehan allowed just one run over 11.2 innings with 15 strikeouts.
“Man, Emmet’s been great. The last two have been fantastic,” Roberts said after he was sent down. “Emmet’s done everything he can do in his power to force our hand, which I love. ... The last two have been really good.”
Now, Sheehan is getting another opportunity to take down bulk innings and audition for a spot on the postseason roster. If he has another strong outing, he'll likely secure a spot in the postseason bullpen as a multi-inning option.
As for Hurt, he's been up and down multiple times this season. The right-hander has made 43 appearances at the big league level, compiling a 4.33 ERA with 56 strikeouts to 23 walks over 43.2 innings of work.
He's unlikely to factor into the team's October plans, but could take down innings over the final week of the regular season.
Dodgers Place Tarik Skubal on Bereavement List, Option Seth Halvorsen
Skubal will deal with a personal matter for the next couple days, but should be back in time to make one more start before the conclusion of the regular season.
He pitched on Saturday, allowing four runs over five innings with three strikeouts.
As for Halvorsen, he's made 11 appearances at the big league level for the Dodgers this season, accruing an 8.10 ERA with six strikeouts to two walks over 10 innings of work.
He was acquired by the Dodgers a couple weeks before the trade deadline in a three-player deal with the Colorado Rockies. He likely won't return to the big league club for the remainder of the year.

item.title: [New York Post] Kyle Tucker out of Dodgers lineup as new injury concern surfaces
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
item.description: Just as Kyle Tucker was finally starting to heat up, he became the latest Dodgers star to suffer a potential injury concern. On Sunday, Tucker was not in the Dodgers’ lineup for their series-finale against the San Francisco Giants, absent a day after he left Saturday’s game early following a foul ball off his right knee/shin area. The good news: Tucker insisted on Sunday that he felt fine and didn’t anticipate it causing ongoing problems. Still, manager Dave Roberts had said Saturday night he ex
item.content:encoded:
Just as Kyle Tucker was finally starting to heat up, he became the latest Dodgers star to suffer a potential injury concern.
On Sunday, Tucker was not in the Dodgers’ lineup for their series-finale against the San Francisco Giants, absent a day after he left Saturday’s game early following a foul ball off his right knee/shin area.
The good news: Tucker insisted on Sunday that he felt fine and didn’t anticipate it causing ongoing problems.
Still, manager Dave Roberts had said Saturday night he expected Tucker in the lineup on Sunday, depending on how the issue progressed.
Tucker initially suffered the injury in the third inning Saturday night, when a foul ball banged high enough up his leg it evaded his shin pad.
The four-time All-Star immediately went down in pain, and was checked out by Roberts and a trainer for several moments.
Initially, Tucker stayed in the game, drawing a walk (and racing around the bases to later score a run) in the fifth while playing out in right field until the seventh.
However, he appeared to be moving around somewhat gingerly after the injury, and was ultimately removed once the score got out of reach in the Dodgers’ eventual 10-4 win.
Postgame, Tucker didn’t seem overly concerned with the issue, saying he should be “good with it” and that the lopsided score was a factor in his precautionary removal.
“I feel like everyone is grinding at this point of the season,” he noted.
On Sunday morning, he echoed that sentiment, saying Roberts had informed him Sunday they were “just gonna at least give me the day.”
The Dodgers will have to hope the injury doesn’t impact Tucker’s recently resurgent performance. In his last 10 games, the $240 million outfielder has finally started to turn a corner, going 15-for-35 with five home runs, nine extra-base hits and 11 RBIs in that stretch.
In 2024, a similar foul ball left Tucker with a right shin fracture that sidelined him for three months.
However, he said this one hit in a different spot of his leg, while once again downplaying the potential severity of the problem.
“This was a little different,” he said. “I feel fine.”

The Los Angeles Dodgers kept right fielder Kyle Tucker out of their lineup for Sunday’s game after he exited Saturday’s win early.
Tucker fouled a ball off of his shin Saturday, and left the game shortly after. Manager Dave Roberts expected Tucker to return to the lineup Sunday, but the outfielder clearly isn’t fit to participate.
Who is Starting for the Dodgers?
The Dodgers are running a bullpen day on Sunday, and could have a few players fill in if needed. Jack Dreyer is getting the ball first for the Dodgers, making his second start of the season. He has a 3.19 ERA through 63 appearances with 68 strikeouts in 59.1 innings pitched.
Emmet Sheehan has a locker at Dodger Stadium as well, and could handle bulk for LA on Sunday.
Who is in the Dodgers’ Lineup?
Shortstop Mookie Betts remains in the leadoff spot for the Dodgers, and center fielder Tommy Edman shoots up the order to bat second. Left fielder Teoscar Hernandez bats third, and first baseman Freddie Freeman serves as the cleanup hitter.
Miguel Rojas enters the lineup as the second baseman and No. 5 hitter, and third baseman Max Muncy slides down the order to the No. 6 spot. Josue De Paula remains the team’s designated hitter, and following him are left fielder Kiké Hernandez and catcher Hunter Feduccia to round out the Dodgers’ lineup.
Dodgers Lineup vs. Giants
1. Mookie Betts, SS
2. Tommy Edman, CF
3. Teoscar Hernandez, LF
4. Freddie Freeman, 1B
5. Miguel Rojas, 2B
6. Max Muncy, 3B
7. Josue De Paula, DH
8. Kiké Hernandez, LF
9. Hunter Feduccia, C
Who is Starting for the Giants?
On the mound for the Giants is left-hander Matt WIlkinson, who will be making his seventh appearance of the year. He has a 4.58 ERA through 19.2 innings pitched, striking out 12 batters durign that time.
The rookie struggled in his first stint as a starter, transitioning to relief for his last two appearances and holding his opponents scoreless.
The Dodgers will look to break his scoreless streak in Sunday’s game, which begins at 1:10 p.m. PT.

item.title: [Dodger Blue] Edwin Díaz shares encouraging update on feel for pitching since returning
item.dc:creator: Matt Borelli
item.description: Edwin Díaz hasn’t lived up to expectations in his first season with the Los Angeles Dodgers, but he is hoping to finish the year on a good note and perhaps emerge as a bigger factor during the playoffs. Since returning from the 15-day injured list over the weekend, the right-hander has thrown two scoreless innings against the San Francisco Giants. In those appearances, he allowed just two baserunners and collected four strikeouts. “Yeah, 100%,” Díaz said when asked if he feels as good as he has
item.content:encoded:
Edwin Díaz hasn’t lived up to expectations in his first season with the Los Angeles Dodgers, but he is hoping to finish the year on a good note and perhaps emerge as a bigger factor during the playoffs.
Since returning from the 15-day injured list over the weekend, the right-hander has thrown two scoreless innings against the San Francisco Giants. In those appearances, he allowed just two baserunners and collected four strikeouts.
“Yeah, 100%,” Díaz said when asked if he feels as good as he has all season. “I’ve been able to throw strikes. That was my problem and concern. I wasn’t throwing my fastball for strike. Now I’m able to command my fastball pretty good. When I command my fastball, my slider plays up. So I feel really good right now.”
Díaz’s success is coming after an uneven rehab assignment with Triple-A Oklahoma City that drew some criticism from manager Dave Roberts. The three-time All-Star gave up five runs in his second-to-last appearance and was reminded that he needed to pitch better.
Díaz bounced back with a scoreless effort after working on some adjustments with Comets pitching coaches Ryan Dennick and David Anderson. It’s still early, but Díaz believes the changes have helped him regain command of his fastball, which had been an issue throughout the season.
“I think my mechanics are better,” Díaz said. “After my rough game in Triple-A, I sat down with the Triple-A pitching coach to see what was the problem. We found I wasn’t moving my hips the right way, so we started working on that.
Díaz further noted his slider is back to being the devastating secondary pitch that he has become known for in his career.
“Yeah, right now it’s really good,” Díaz said. “It’s going down and away. I’ve been able to throw my fastball glove side, and if I throw my fastball glove side, [the slider] will play up in the same path.”
Edwin Díaz benefiting from new role
Prior to rejoining the Dodgers, Roberts made it clear that Díaz would not be returning to the closer role anytime soon as a way to ease him back into action. Both of his appearances against the Giants came in low-leverage situations, and Díaz believes that approach has helped him thrive so far.
“Yeah, yeah. I have an open mind. I’m in the situation right now where I need to help this team to win,” Díaz explained. “Whenever Doc puts me in the game, in any situation, I will do my job. And I feel good. I just want to keep climbing the ladder and finish the season strong.”

This browser does not support the video element.
LOS ÁNGELES -- Podría no pasar tanto tiempo antes de que Shohei Ohtani esté de regreso para encabezar la alineación de los Dodgers.
Tras otro día productivo en su progresión de bateo, Ohtani (bíceps derecho, rodilla izquierda) se sigue perfilando a ser activado de la lista de lesionados de 15 días durante la próxima serie de los Dodgers contra los Padres, informó el dirigente Dave Roberts tras la victoria del sábado por la noche 10-4 sobre los Gigantes en el Dodger Stadium.
"Hay una buena posiblidad de que lo veamos en la próxima serie", expresó Roberts.
El paso de Ohtani a la lista de lesionados de 15 días es retroactivo al 8 de septiembre, lo que significa que es elegible para ser activado el miércoles, el segundo encuentro de la última serie en casa de los bicampeones contra los Frailes. Regresará estrictamente como bateador, debido a que está descartado para lanzar.
Luego de comenzar una progresión de bateo el martes, Ohtani ya avanzó a batear frente a la máquina Trajekt, la cual simula enfrentar a verdaderos lanzadores. Salió sintiéndose bien tras realizar entre 30 y 40 swings el sábado, indicó Roberts. Ohtani también corrió las bases mientras la escuadra de Los Ángeles realizaba las prácticas de bateo en el terreno.
Ohtani registró OPS de .902 y encabezó el equipo con 30 jonrones antes de que sus persistentes lesiones en el bíceps derecho y la rodilla izquierda lo obligaran a apartarse. En sus 24 encuentros antes de ingresar a la lista de lesionados, que coincidió con un intento de intensificar su trabajo en el montículo, Ohtani bateó .198 (de 96-19) con 34 ponches en 96 turnos.
Si Ohtani regresa cuando sea elegible el miércoles, solo contará con cinco partidos de temporada regular para volverse a acoplar a la acción de las Grandes Ligas antes de la postemporada.
Los Dodgers han estado sin Ohtani en el lineup en 15 de sus últimos 16 compromisos, pero han encontrado su ritmo incluso sin su mejor bateador, consiguiendo marca de 13-3 en ese trecho.

item.title: [cbssports.com] Dodgers eye sweep of Giants behind surging Mookie Betts
item.dc:creator: FLM
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers will continue getting their house in order when they face the San Francisco Giants on Sunday afternoon to complete the Dodgers' next-to-last home series of the regular season. Los Angeles will use a bullpen game Sunday when it seeks a three-game series sweep, while the Giants will send left-hander Matt Wilkinson (1-3, 4.58 ERA) to the mound for his first appearance against the Dodgers. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers will continue getting their house in order when they face the San Francisco Giants on Sunday afternoon to complete the Dodgers' next-to-last home series of the regular season.
Los Angeles will use a bullpen game Sunday when it seeks a three-game series sweep, while the Giants will send left-hander Matt Wilkinson (1-3, 4.58 ERA) to the mound for his first appearance against the Dodgers.
Los Angeles has a lot of uncertainty heading into its 14th consecutive playoff appearance -- including the rotation because Blake Snell is working through groin discomfort -- while the offense has Shohei Ohtani (biceps inflammation, knee soreness) and Andy Pages (left hand fracture) nearing a return from the injured list.
The revival of Mookie Betts, along with the arrival of Josue De Paula from the minor leagues, has brought renewed energy after a mid-summer swoon.
The Dodgers still do not have a return date for Ohtani, with Betts the latest to claim the star's leadoff spot. Betts had two home runs among his three hits as the leadoff hitter Friday, then returned to the top spot Saturday and went 4-for-4 with three doubles and a walk. He has 10 hits over his past three games.
"The main thing is doing it when it counts," Betts said. "So right now, we just keep laying the foundation, and then when playoffs come, just need it to show up (offensively)."
Betts had an RBI single in the second inning and an RBI double in the fourth Saturday as the Dodgers earned a 10-4 victory over the Giants.
"He's not a chase guy anyway, but he's cut that down considerably," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. "The quality of contact is considerably higher. And then now you've got that attitude, that confidence, that we're used to seeing with Mookie."
The Dodgers' Will Smith also is rounding into form after missing three months with neck inflammation. Smith returned at the start of September and has three home runs over his past nine games, including one in each of the past two games.
Smith started consecutive games Friday and Saturday for the third time since he returned, although he is expected to be used off the bench, if at all, on Sunday.
The Giants have their own injury concerns. Ace Logan Webb was the latest to see his season end early, due to a blister on his right middle finger.
On Saturday, first baseman Bryce Eldridge missed his second consecutive game with a head laceration. The 6-foot-7 rookie bumped his head on a low overhang at the team hotel.
"He's still feeling the implications of that deal," Giants manager Tony Vitello said Saturday. "It's kind of a weird spot in the hotel. I checked it out. (Friday) it was a little bit more about just his comfort. But now, stemming from last night and this morning, those guys have been monitoring him like crazy. Just some lingering effects."
Giants rookie Victor Bericoto hit a two-run home run Saturday in his second game since returning from the injured list and now has five homers in 35 career games.
With a win Sunday, the Dodgers can earn their first three-game sweep over the Giants since April 2024. Los Angeles leads the season series 5-4, with one game remaining in L.A. and three games at San Francisco to end the regular season.

item.title: [Dodger Blue] Dave Roberts acknowledges Dodgers still have big need for postseason
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Abdón Ibarra
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers clinched their 13th National League West title in the last 14 seasons, and now all that remains to do is stay in front of the Atlanta Braves down the stretch to secure a first-round bye. “It’s always helpful in the sense of giving your guys a break to reset. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers clinched their 13th National League West title in the last 14 seasons, and now all that remains to do is stay in front of the Atlanta Braves down the stretch to secure a first-round bye.
“It’s always helpful in the sense of giving your guys a break to reset. But given all the tax and where our guys are health-wise, to get that week would be huge,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts recently said. “We’ve still got to play well to finish out the season to get to that point. There’s a lot of people that could use the break.”
The Dodgers have a four-game lead over the Braves for the second seed in the NL. L.A. needs to finish with a better record than the Braves by virtue of not holding the head-to-head tiebreaker.
The top seed in the NL is within reach for the Dodgers, but they do not control their own destiny due to trailing the Milwaukee Brewers in the standings. Furthermore, the Dodgers also don’t have the tiebreaker over the Brewers.
Securing home-field advantage throughout the postseason would certainly be of value, but finishing as one of the top two division winners in the NL is of greater importance.
Some of the notable injuries the Dodgers are dealing with include Shohei Ohtani, Edgardo Henriquez, Andy Pages, Will Klein and, most recently, Blake Snell.
The Wild Card Series begins Tuesday, Sept. 29, while the NL Division Series starts Saturday, Oct. 3.
Pages and Ohtani are expected to be activated prior to the regular season concluding, and there is optimism Snell will avoid going on the injured list.
Henriquez is eligible to return on the same day the Wild Card round begins. Meanwhile, Klein can’t return until the NLDS starts. It is not a given that the Dodgers would elect to have Klein on their postseason roster given his two-month absence, but they would still prefer to have the option.
Dodgers postseason outlook
Should the Dodgers remain the No. 2 seed in the NL postseason bracket, they would face the Wild Card winner of the matchup between the third division champion and sixth-place team. However, who that could be is still very much in question in part because of a late surge from the San Diego Padres.
The Chicago Cubs, Philadelphia Phillies and Padres are all in a dead heat and mathematically possible of slotting into any order as the three Wild Card teams.

item.title: [FanSided] Edwin Díaz’s brilliant return should make Dodgers haters very, very nervous
item.dc:creator: Jake Elman
item.description: Only the Los Angeles Dodgers could have a $69 million All-Star closer as a potential hidden weapon ahead of the postseason. item.content:encoded:
Only the Los Angeles Dodgers could have a $69 million All-Star closer as a potential hidden weapon ahead of the postseason.
Such a thing shouldn’t be possible, but the Dodgers aren’t most teams. Friday night’s blowout win over the Giants presented what’s been a rare sight this year: Edwin Díaz taking the mound in the ninth inning. The 32-year-old has missed much of the season with elbow and neck problems, and the 8-2 rout marked his first outing since Aug. 17.
Díaz pitching a scoreless ninth in September is exactly what Dodgers fans envisioned when they added the three-time All-Star this past offseason. However, manager Dave Roberts confirmed that Díaz, who had recorded an 11.85 ERA and allowed 10 walks in his first 14.2 innings, will not move back into the closer role.
In fact, Roberts admitted he would not have used the veteran reliever on Friday night if not for the team's six-run lead. To his credit, Díaz worked around a two-out single, and his fastball averaged 97.6 mph, which MLB's Sarah Wexler reported was up 1.3 mph from his season average.
“I think we just want to see him throw the baseball the way he's capable of,” Roberts said. “And you’re talking about nine games, so you're talking three or four outings to evaluate, and that should be adequate.”
The story was much the same on Saturday: L.A. calling on Diaz in a six-run game, and Diaz striking out two batters with just one baserunner in a scoreless inning — all while looking much more like the guy the Dodgers thought they were acquiring this offseason.
Could Edwin Díaz actually help the Los Angeles Dodgers in the postseason?
If the postseason began Sunday, the Dodgers would be the NL’s No. 2 seed and have a first-round bye. They’d then host the highest remaining seed in the NLDS, which would either be the NL East-leading Braves or the No. 6 seed (the Phillies held that spot entering Sunday, though they are one game back of the No. 4 Cubs and No. 5 Padres).
Wexler wrote that Díaz is competing for a spot on the playoff roster, which isn’t overly surprising to anyone familiar with Roberts’ mindset. Financial commitments and a player’s Baseball-Reference pages only matter so much, and the Dodgers have three championships in the last six years to prove it.
Roberts, who took over the Dodgers ahead of the 2016 season, has spent the last decade proving he’s not afraid to bench underperforming players or go with the hot hand. If Díaz returns to his earlier form and is dreadful over the team’s final seven games, it's difficult to imagine he’d be a lock to make the 26-man playoff roster.
The reality is that neither Roberts nor the Dodgers know what they’ll get from Díaz, who already has four games where he's given up at least three runs. He’s been worth -1.2 bWAR in 17 games, and he allowed five runs, three walks and a hit by pitch during a recent Triple-A outing during his rehab stint.
Personally, we’re skeptical about Díaz making a significant positive difference if he makes the postseason roster. Two low-stress outings don't make up for an entire season's worth of dysfunction. But the velocity is now creeping back up into the high 90s, and that's an awfully promising sign. We need to see him keep doing it over the final week of the regular season, but if he can, that could answer this team's most pressing question entering October.
Díaz has silenced his critics in the past, most notably after an ugly first season with the Mets in 2019. Hey, we were willing to own our prediction that the Nationals would lose at least 110 games. Prove us wrong, Edwin!

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants, 10-4, on Saturday night and improved to 95-60 on the year.
Left-hander Tarik Skubal had an uncharacteristic start, striking out just three batters over five innings while allowing four earned runs. Fortunately, the bullpen picked him up with four scoreless innings.
Offensively, Mookie Betts had a marvelous four-hit night and Will Smith notched three hits of his own, including a home run. Rookie Josue De Paula continued to impress with two walks and a two-run single with the bases loaded.
After the game, manager Dave Roberts provided an update on Shohei Ohtani, saying he has a "good chance" of being activated during the team's series against the San Diego Padres this week.
While Ohtani is eligible to be activated on Wednesday, it's currently unclear if that's the day he'll be back.
Either way, the Dodgers are expecting Ohtani back soon, and he took a major step on Saturday, hitting off the Trajekt machine and running the bases before the game.
In his stead, De Paula has done an unbelievable job as the everyday designated hitter.
In other news, the Dodgers recently promoted an outfielder who previously thought that his season might be over. The third-round pick in the 2024 MLB Draft was hitting .306 with a .985 OPS across 35 games in High-A and 71 appearances in Double-A this season.
Finally, veteran outfielder Teoscar Hernández was recently labeled as a likely trade candidate by Pat Ragazzo of FanSided. The insider explained that the influx of outfield talent, combined with an expiring contract that was reportedly being shopped around over the offseason, could lead to the team parting ways with "Mr. Seeds."
"The Dodgers have No. 1 prospect Josue De Paula and other young outfielders in their farm system, who could replace Hernandez in left field next season," Ragazzo wrote. "It would make sense for the Dodgers to ship Hernandez out this offseason with one-year remaining on his deal."

item.title: [Just Baseball] Is Blake Snell the Dodgers’ Best Pitcher Right Now? | Just Baseball
item.dc:creator: Ryan Murphy
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers have done it again. With the Dodgers’ win on Thursday afternoon, they officially clinched the NL West championship for the fifth consecutive year. This marks the Dodgers’ 13th NL West title out of the past 14 years, with their lone second place finish coming in 2021 behind an otherworldly season from the San Francisco Giants. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have done it again.
With the Dodgers’ win on Thursday afternoon, they officially clinched the NL West championship for the fifth consecutive year. This marks the Dodgers’ 13th NL West title out of the past 14 years, with their lone second place finish coming in 2021 behind an otherworldly season from the San Francisco Giants.
It has been an interesting season for this Dodgers team. After a scorching hot 56-30 start through June, the Dodgers slumped to a 26-25 record in July and August. Now hunting for the top seed in the National League for the postseason, the Dodgers have bounced back to an 11-5 record in September (as of Thursday).
A major factor in the Dodgers’ volatility this year has been their susceptibility to injury. This year alone, a whopping 27 players have seen time on the Dodgers’ injured list.
The majority of these players have made their way back from the injured list, to varying degrees of success. Of those who have returned to the active roster, one player stands above them all.
Starter Blake Snell has been on a tear since his return from the injured list. While his status moving forward is now in question following his early exit from his September 16 start against the Cincinnati Reds, his run of dominance has been a sight to behold.
Yet, for Snell, the journey to get to this point has been far from a walk in the park.
Stats as of September 17.
Celebrations and Setbacks
Snell came into the 2026 season as arguably the co-ace of the Dodgers’ starting rotation, alongside Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
The left-hander had been a pivotal part of the Dodgers’ 2025 World Series run, allowing just two runs over his first 21 innings of work. Snell cooled off significantly in the World Series, allowing 10 earned runs over 13 innings, but he was invaluable to the Dodgers nonetheless.
However, Snell’s heavy usage in October had some untoward downstream effects. Left with minimal recovery time between the end of the season and the beginning of spring training, Snell had difficulty getting ramped back up for the year. As a result, his offseason throwing progression suffered unanticipated delays.
Lingering shoulder fatigue kept Snell off of the mound through early May, missing the first 38 games. Finally, nearly a month and a half into the 2026 season, Snell was set to make his season debut. Unfortunately for Snell and the Dodgers, his return was interrupted almost immediately.
After three innings against the Atlanta Braves on May 9, Snell’s season debut was done. He allowed four earned runs, striking out five batters while allowing six hits and two walks. Unbeknownst to Snell, this would be his last start for over three months.
Snell was scratched from his next scheduled start. Just one day later, he underwent surgery to remove loose bodies from his left elbow. As a result, Snell missed another 78 games, finally making his return in early August. Since then, he seems to have unlocked a new level.
Second-Half Hero
Snell has long been known to elevate his game during the second half of each season. For his career, he has posted a 3.96 ERA in the first half and a 2.31 ERA during the latter half. As good as his career second-half numbers may be, he’s been even better in his return to the mound this year.
Over his last seven starts, Snell has pitched to an incredible 1.01 ERA, recording 47 strikeouts and 14 walks over 35.2 innings. Opponents are batting a measly .164/.254/.205 against him, and he has allowed no more than one run in any start during this span.
With a sample this small, it is difficult to quantify just how effective Snell has been compared to his Dodgers teammates. This is especially true given the run their starting rotation has been on in recent weeks.
Both Yamamoto and the Dodgers’ marquee trade deadline pickup, Tarik Skubal, have been dominant in their own right. Since Snell returned to the rotation on August 11, Yamamoto and Skubal have each posted an ERA under 2.10 over 30+ innings apiece.
Still, Snell’s ERA over the same span clears both of theirs by a full run. Though Skubal narrowly edges out Snell in fWAR (1.8 fWAR vs. 1.7 fWAR), Snell’s success is all the more unprecedented given this is his first sustained stretch of play since the 2025 postseason.
Expanding beyond just the Dodgers, Snell’s metrics stack up well among the league’s best. Among all qualified pitchers over the same span, Snell holds the second-best ERA, third-best FIP, second-best fWAR, and third-best K/9 rate. He is the only qualified pitcher to have yet to surrender a home run over this span.
What’s Been Working?
Since returning from the IL, Snell has demonstrated a number of improvements.
For one, his stuff seems to have jumped in effectiveness. Every one of Snell’s pitches has seen either a marginal or significant jump in induced movement.
In particular, his fastball has gained nearly an inch of both induced vertical break and horizontal break. This pairs incredibly well with his improved curveball, which has gained two inches of depth and over an inch of horizontal movement.
Factoring in his slider and changeup, Snell’s arsenal has looked remarkably effective as a whole. As a result, his two best pitches have played up in a big way. Though the sample is small, Snell’s fastball has allowed just a 5.6% hard-hit percentage. While batters hit .309 and slugged .426 against his heater in 2025, those figures have dropped to .179 and .232 so far this year.
The results on his curveball have been even more effective, as batters are batting and slugging .086 against it. In 37 plate appearances, hitters have recorded just three hits against Snell’s curveball compared to 20 strikeouts. He has yet to allow an extra-base hit with his curveball in 2026.
Beyond Snell’s improved arsenal, he has also located the ball well. A pitcher with Snell’s profile traditionally operates best working around the edges of the strike zone. This allows him to induce whiffs and chase swings, leading to a higher strikeout rate and more frequent weak contact, but also more walks.
Snell has leaned into this philosophy, attacking early while working around the edges later in at-bats. He has thrown fewer balls in the zone overall, improving his chase rate, but has also significantly increased his first-pitch strike percentage.
Room for Concern
Snell’s run of dominance has been impressive, to say the least. But, his most recent start brings a sobering point to the conversation around his performance.
Last year, the Dodgers leaned heavily on Snell at the end of the regular season and the postseason. He did not bounce back gracefully, missing over 100 games in the 2026 season.
This year, the Dodgers hope to lean on Snell heavily once again as they approach October baseball. As such, it is reasonable to air concerns around the volatility of his health, with his most recent start as an example.
Snell left after one inning against the Reds, citing a left groin issue. In years past, Snell has missed anywhere from a few weeks to a couple of months battling the same issue.
However, he did frame his decision to exit the game as precautionary, rather than reactive. According to Snell, he felt the area tighten up during his pre-game bullpen, and he felt it was best not to push it. While he still hopes to make his next start, nobody can know for sure what the full impact of this issue will wind up being.
The Dodgers have yet to make any further announcements around the injury. At this time, Snell has not been placed on the injured list either. The first real test will be whether Snell ends up making his next start. Manager Dave Roberts has weighed the idea of delaying it, but any deviation from the norm will have an impact at this stage.
Whether Snell remains healthy through October is anybody’s guess. Regardless, his remarkable performance since coming back from injury is a testament to both his talent and resilience. Hopefully, fans can look forward to Snell making a comeback against the San Diego Padres next week.

item.title: [pasadenastarnews.com] Mookie Betts stays hot as Dodgers hammer Giants
item.dc:creator: Doug Padilla
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Mookie Betts is showing that the view from the top offers a wide range of possibilities. Hitting in Shohei Ohtani’s leadoff spot for the second consecutive game, Betts’ four-hit performance on Saturday night topped his three-hit output from Friday and started some serious downhill momentum toward a 10-4 victory over the San Francisco Giants. The victory kept the Dodgers (95-60) two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers (97-58) for the best record in the National League and four games
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Mookie Betts is showing that the view from the top offers a wide range of possibilities.
Hitting in Shohei Ohtani’s leadoff spot for the second consecutive game, Betts’ four-hit performance on Saturday night topped his three-hit output from Friday and started some serious downhill momentum toward a 10-4 victory over the San Francisco Giants.
The victory kept the Dodgers (95-60) two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers (97-58) for the best record in the National League and four games ahead of the Atlanta Braves (91-64) for the No. 2 playoff seed with seven games remaining. That includes four games against the Giants, who continue to limp toward the finish line of a miserable, injury-riddled season.
Betts couldn’t be feeling better, with his past two games part of a run of 10 hits over the last three games he has played. After more than two months of looking for an offensive leader, Betts has charged into the role, while reaching base five times on Saturday.
“It’s good; It’s fun,” Betts said. “But the main thing is doing it when it counts. So right now, we just keep laying the foundation, and then when playoffs come, we just need it to show up (offensively).”
The Dodgers expect Ohtani to return for the playoffs as he makes progress from biceps and knee discomfort. Betts, though, is proving to be a more-than-adequate emergency replacement.
“You know, I couldn’t tell you that I saw this (coming), but I just felt that he was stronger,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. “He’s worked hard on that. He looks great. He’s not going to stop working, and just for it to come together has been great, and I think for me it’s just trying to keep him confident.”
The Dodgers also have been transformed by the emergence of catcher Will Smith, who returned at the start of September after three months away because of neck inflammation. He had a home run among his three hits Saturday to give him homers in consecutive games, with three over his past eight contests.
“He’ll play two or three that last series (at San Francisco), but yeah, after that, he’ll be our guy (for the playoffs),” Roberts said.
There is also 21-year-old rookie Josue De Paula, who has continued to operate with ease since arriving in the major leagues last week. De Paula had a two-run single Saturday and walked twice while scoring two runs.
All of it overshadowed Tarik Skubal’s ninth start for the Dodgers. The two-time American League Cy Young Award winner was far from his best, allowing four runs on eight hits over five innings. His three strikeouts were his least in an outing with his new club.
Skubal unleashed his frustrations in the dugout by throwing his glove and cap at the bench, while firing an empty sports drink bottle at the wall.
“Sometimes you get frustrated and you got to get it out,” Skubal said. “It’s no good just keeping it pent up. So yeah, I’m a believer in getting that stuff out and kind of just moving on from the moment. The frustration is based on execution and knowing who I am and I’m just not doing that.”
Skubal blamed a lack of fastball command for the inability to shut down the Giants.
“Not driving it up and in (and) kind of pulling the ball down at times, pushing it up at times,” Skubal said. “I think pitching is almost all fastball command and mine wasn’t great today.”
And yet the offense allowed Skubal (11-7) to pick up the win, while improving to 4-2 with a 2.95 ERA for the Dodgers.
“That’s our job. That’s what we’re supposed to do,” Betts said. “So sometimes it’s them, sometimes it’s us. As long as we win.”
Kyle Tucker provided a scare when he fouled a ball off the side of his right knee early in the game then departed in the seventh inning with the Dodgers leading by six runs. Tucker reached base twice Saturday after collecting six hits with two home runs the previous two games.
“Whatever’s working at the time, you just ride it out, whether or not it’s the way you want to go about it,” said Tucker, who expects to play Sunday. “If it’s working, it’s working. You just try to go up there and put up competitive at-bats and just do your part on defense.”
The offense was not only productive, it was steady. The Dodgers scored runs in each of the first six innings and when they were held scoreless in the seventh, Betts still reached base with a walk.
Betts opened the game for the Dodgers with a leadoff double and scored on a Max Muncy double. Betts brought home his own run with an RBI single in the second.
The Dodgers struck with Smith’s home run in the third and got an RBI double from Betts in the fourth but were still tied 4-4 heading into the bottom of the fifth. They blew the game open from there, getting a go-ahead two-run single from Tommy Edman and an RBI pinch-hit single from Miguel Rojas for a 7-4 lead.
They scored three more times in the sixth, getting a Smith RBI single followed by a two-run single from De Paula.
“I think this is the first time, seems like all year, that we’ve had four or five hitters swing the bats well for four or five games,” Roberts said. “So it’s been really good to see. Obviously, Mookie is a big part of it, but everyone else is doing their part.”
The Dodgers now have a 5-4 lead in the Giants in the season series and are in line for a sweep on Sunday, which would be their first against their longtime rival since April of 2024.

item.title: [New York Post] Mookie Betts thriving batting first: Should he hit leadoff for Dodgers instead of Shohei Ohtani?

item.content:encoded:
Plan A, as always, is Shohei Ohtani.
But over the last couple nights, Plan B has looked pretty good too.
Whenever Ohtani returns from the injured list, the two-way star will likely reprise his customary role as the Dodgers’ leadoff hitter –– one he has held since halfway through his debut 2024 season with the team.
Likely, however, was as far as manager Dave Roberts was willing to describe it on Saturday.
Because in Ohtani’s absence, Mookie Betts has made a case to spearhead the team’s order, too.
Over the last week, a red-hot Betts has served as the Dodgers’ leadoff hitter three times. In each of those contests, he delivered a vintage performance.
There was a 2-for-4 display with an RBI and a double in Miami last week.
A 3-for-4 outburst with two home runs (including one to lead off the game) against the San Francisco Giants on Friday night.
Then, a 4-for-4, three-double, two-RBI, one-walk masterpiece in another 10-4 rout of the Giants on Saturday, a victory that lowered the Dodgers’ magic number to clinch a first-round playoff bye down to four with eight days remaining in the season.
“I just think he’s physically in a better spot than he has been,” Roberts said after Saturday’s outburst, which pushed Betts’ season average up to .261 and OPS to .785. “The ball’s coming off the right way.”
Of course, Betts has been crushing the ball regardless of where he’s been in the order lately. Since Aug. 5, he is batting .336 in 39 games with nine home runs, 12 doubles, 31 RBIs and a 1.008 OPS.
It has marked the former MVP’s best extended stretch since early in the 2024 season. It has been a reminder that there’s still plenty of life left in his previously slumping bat.
“I know I’m still capable of it,” the 33-year-old Betts said. “I know it was in there somewhere.”
Added Roberts: “It just doesn’t matter where you hit him, who he’s facing, [what’s] the situation –– he’s taking good at-bats.”
Betts’ impact at the top of the lineup specifically, however, has been impossible to ignore over the last week; especially when juxtaposed with the ongoing uncertainty surrounding Ohtani, who is expected back next week from right arm and left knee injuries but still doesn’t figure to be 100% physically.
That’s why, after writing Betts’ name in at the leadoff spot for a second-straight day Saturday, Roberts was asked if it’s still a certainty that Ohtani will remain in the leadoff spot upon his return.
“Yeah, I mean, I think that’s my first kind of thought,” Roberts said. “But until he gets back, or when he gets back, then I’ll kind of potentially read and react.”
Much will obviously depend on how Ohtani looks, which will be the biggest question after a 6-for-52 slump leading up to his IL stint.
Roberts also cited other factors like trying to match up against either right- or left-handed pitching, leaving the door open to some game-by-game tinkering in October.
“I haven’t really thought too much about it [yet],” he insisted.
The way Betts is going, though, it might soon become a critical lineup-construction decision.
Run the risk with a potentially diminished but ever-dangerous Ohtani? Or give the most at-bats as possible to the team’s hottest current hitter?
Granted, Betts hasn’t pushed to take over the leadoff spot, saying Friday that “I’ll hit wherever” and “there’s a guy that’s named Shohei that needs to be up there and to get us going.”
But if the Dodgers need to pivot among Ohtani’s ongoing ailments, he is quickly emerging as their best fallback option –– especially with their initial leadoff replacement, the switch-hitting Tommy Edman, mired in a brutal 2-for-39 slump.
“Going back up there, it is fun,” Betts acknowledged, having played almost 1,100 career games as a leadoff hitter over his 13-year career. “Kind of feels like home.”
“You do got to kind of prepare for whatever,” Roberts added, “and I just think that Mookie’s swinging the bat well, has hit there many times throughout his career, so it just kind of makes sense.”
For now, the Dodgers’ bigger priority will be making sure Betts keeps swinging the bat well, whether that’s in the No. 1 spot or somewhere else in the heart of the order.
His late-season surge has been one of the biggest reasons the team has survived Ohtani’s absence –– winning 13 of its last 16 despite the superstar slugger playing in just one of those contests.
“It’s good. It’s fun. But the main thing is doing it when it counts,” Betts said of his recent success. “Right now, just keep laying the foundation, and then when playoffs come, just need it to show up.”
Still, given how things are trending at the moment, it might not be a surprise if the Dodgers’ first at-bat of the playoffs belonged to their streaking shortstop.
“I couldn’t tell you that I saw this [coming],” Roberts conceded. “But he’s got stronger. He’s worked hard on that … And just for it to come together has been great.”

item.content:encoded:
Mookie conecta cuatro hits y los Dodgers se llevan la serie ante Gigantes
This browser does not support the video element.
LOS ÁNGELES -- La manera en que Mookie Betts ha estado bateando últimamente recuerda a sus mejores días como jugador de los Dodgers.
Betts remolcó dos carreras y anotó otras dos en una actuación de cuatro hits, mientras Los Ángeles superaba a San Francisco, 10-4, la noche del sábado en el Dodger Stadium, preparando el escenario para una oportunidad de barrer la serie del fin de semana.
En enfrentamientos directos de todos los tiempos, los Dodgers tienen una ventaja de un juego, 1,293-1,292, con 17 empates, sobre sus rivales de muchos años.
Días antes, antes de que los Dodgers aseguraran su 13er título de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional en las últimas 14 temporadas, el manager Dave Roberts evaluó la situación de su equipo con la postemporada cada vez más cerca. Elogió el desempeño de su cuerpo de lanzadores y destacó las mejoras en la defensa y el corrido de bases. Pero también señaló un área por mejorar: la ofensiva, que ha sido inconsistente durante buena parte de la temporada.
“Creo que, para mí, se trata de poder liquidar a los equipos cuando tenemos oportunidades”, dijo Roberts, haciéndose eco de sentimientos similares que había expresado durante los últimos tres meses.
Los Dodgers aprovecharon esas oportunidades el sábado, y su tercera victoria consecutiva mantuvo su ventaja de cuatro juegos sobre los Bravos por el No. 2 en la Liga Nacional.
En una noche en la que Tarik Skubal batalló durante sus cinco innings y permitió cuatro carreras, su mayor cantidad desde el 24 de junio, su ofensiva estuvo ahí para respaldarlo. Todo comenzó con Betts como primer bate, un puesto que ha sido una especie de puerta giratoria con Shohei Ohtani en la lista de lesionados.
Betts se embasó en sus cinco apariciones al plato por primera vez desde el 16 de abril de 2024. Conectó tres dobles, marcando la primera vez que registra tres extrabases en un juego desde el 7 de julio de 2023. Y ha conectado al menos tres hits en tres juegos consecutivos, igualando la racha más larga de su carrera, también del 11 al 17 de julio de 2021.
No han sido solamente tres buenos días para Betts. En septiembre, batea para .397/.493/.794, con 20 carreras impulsadas, la mayor cantidad del equipo. Si nos remontamos aún más, tiene un OPS de 1.008 en sus últimos 39 juegos.

item.title: [whittierdailynews.com] Dodgers’ Andy Pages on track to return Tuesday

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Andy Pages went through the paces on Saturday afternoon, grinding through an intense on-field workout in the clearest sign yet that he will be ready to return on Tuesday to open the final home series of the regular season.
Pages wore a fitness tracker, similar to what soccer players use to monitor all aspects of physical fitness. Coaches and staff put him through an estimated five simulated innings all in a compressed window of time.
The All-Star center fielder not only tested his broken left hand, but he also pushed his physical fitness to the limits.
Pages went from hitting to defense to base running and then doing it all over again to make sure he is ready for the rigors of play next week. His return is expected to come in the opener of a three-game series against the San Diego Padres.
While that kind of energy output is typically done in a rehab game, there aren’t many minor league options remaining this late in the season.
One thing Pages will not get is the chance to hit off a pitcher at full velocity.
“I think that from what I understand, we don’t have really any available arms,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said about the prospect of a live batting practice session. “A lot of our guys are playing in playoff games in the minors, and we have (Eric) Lauer, who’s on the IL. So, we don’t really have anyone.”
That’s not ideal for a player coming off the uncertainty that comes with a hand injury. But Pages did show that his hand soreness has subsided enough to hit multiple balls over the outfield wall.
“I’m expecting good at-bats,” Roberts said. “I can’t speak to the performance. I just want him to have good at-bats, and I’m not sure where he’s going to hit. Somewhere middle to the bottom (of the order), I think. I think I’m waiting just like you guys are waiting to see how it looks.”
The Dodgers close the season with six consecutive games, including the season-ending series in San Francisco next weekend.
“Six in a row, and that seems pretty aggressive (for Pages),” Roberts said. “So, I think that we do want to get him as many at-bats as possible, but we have to make sure that his legs are under him, feeling good, so we don’t go backward or get injured in that respect. It is going to be a balancing act and just keeping a keen eye on Andy, for sure.”
Regardless of what his swing looks like, the Dodgers still trust him in center field. After all, his World Series-saving catch in Game 7 last season came as a late-inning defensive replacement.
“Playing a premium position and playing it well is hugely important,” Roberts said.
ROTATING THE ROTATION
Left-hander Blake Snell is not expected to pitch in the upcoming series against the Padres, but he has not been ruled out for the series against the Giants next weekend.
Snell left his start Thursday after one inning in Cincinnati because of groin discomfort.
“He’s trending very well,” Roberts said about Snell’s recovery in recent days.
Right-hander Roki Sasaki is expected to pitch in the upcoming series against the Padres, although his role has not yet been specified. There is a chance Sasaki could start a game against San Diego, or come out of the bullpen, which had been his expected role in the postseason.
“It will be multiples for sure,” Roberts said about Sasaki’s innings count. “I just don’t know exactly when.”
A LEADING MAN
Shohei Ohtani is still expected to return to play before the regular season ends next Sunday, although there remains no target date.
In the meantime, the Dodgers continue to weigh their options in the leadoff spot. Tommy Edman was there immediately after Ohtani went on the injured list earlier this month, Josue De Paula took a turn there and Mookie Betts has been the latest to stake a claim.
Betts hit two home runs from the leadoff spot Friday and was back at the top of the lineup on Saturday.
“Yeah, I think that certainly there is an uncertainty with Shohei, all the while expecting him to be back,” Roberts said. “But you do got to kind of prepare for whatever, and I just think that Mookie’s swinging the bat well, has hit there many times throughout his career, so it just kind of makes sense.”
Betts had three hits Wednesday in Cincinnati and three more Friday against the Giants in the leadoff spot, including two home runs. He is batting .356 with six home runs and 18 RBIs in 15 September games.
ALSO
The Dodgers are expected to select a pitcher to pick up bulk innings on Sunday in a hybrid bullpen game against the Giants, but the exact plan remains undetermined.
UP NEXT
Giants (LHP Matt Wilkinson, 1-3, 4.58 ERA) at Dodgers (TBA), Sunday, 1:10 p.m., SportsNet LA, 570 AM, 1020 AM

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Dodgers' September surge continues: L.A. racks up 15 hits in win over Giants
item.dc:creator: Maddie Lee
item.description: - Click here to listen to this article - - Mookie Betts hits three doubles and the Dodgers surge for 15 hits to overcome a shaky start by Tarik Skubal in a 10-4 win over the San Francisco Giants. When Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said earlier this week that the best was yet to come, his expectations were centered on the offense. In the Dodgers’ 10-4 rout of the San Francisco Giants on Saturday, that better version of the offense was on display, putting together a pair of three-run rallies
item.content:encoded:
- Click here to listen to this article
-
- Mookie Betts hits three doubles and the Dodgers surge for 15 hits to overcome a shaky start by Tarik Skubal in a 10-4 win over the San Francisco Giants.
When Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said earlier this week that the best was yet to come, his expectations were centered on the offense.
In the Dodgers’ 10-4 rout of the San Francisco Giants on Saturday, that better version of the offense was on display, putting together a pair of three-run rallies in back-to-back innings to take pressure off the pitching staff.
Before that breakout started in the fifth inning, it was a back-and-forth game.
Dodgers left-handed starting pitcher Tarik Skubal pitched only five innings, tied for his shortest start with the Dodgers. And he surrendered four runs, the worst mark of his Dodgers tenure.
Tyler Glasnow hasn’t had the greatest of seasons, but the Dodgers will need him to deliver in the playoffs if they want to win another World Series title.
Entering the game, Skubal appeared to be peaking. His last two starts, both against the Reds, were some of his most efficient.
That efficiency, however, regressed against the Giants (64-91).
Though he got through the first two innings without giving up a run — thanks in part to a diving catch by right fielder Kyle Tucker made in the gap to end the first — he issued two-out walks in each.
The Dodgers’ offense used that time to mount a lead. Leadoff hitter Mookie Betts, who finished the day with three doubles and a single, hit the first of those doubles in his first at-bat, and Max Muncy authored his own to drive in the first run.
The next inning, rookie Josue De Paula’s walk, and singles from Alex Freeland and Betts combined to push in another run.
Then Skubal began to struggle. With a runner on second and one out, he pitched to a full count against designated hitter Victor Bericoto. Skubal missed down the middle with a fastball, and Bericoto sent it 425 feet to center field. It landed on the netting on the other side of the wall to tie the score.
The Dodgers’ offense, coming alive in September, struck back in the third. Catcher Will Smith hit his second home run in as many nights, launching the second pitch of the frame into left-field stands.
The Giants took a different approach to tie the score for a second time. After back-to-back singles, they used back-to-back sacrifice bunts to advance the runners and score another run.
Then the two teams traded runs again. Betts put the Dodgers (95-60) up with an RBI double in the fourth. Skubal gave up back-to-back doubles in the fifth.
That marked both the end of Skubal’s start and the beginning of the Dodgers’ offensive onslaught.
If the man trying to revive the Montreal Expos as an expansion team succeeds, Dan Evans is his choice for president of baseball operations.
The Dodgers brought seven batters to the plate in the fifth, and all but one reached base. Tommy Edman hit a two-run single. And pinch-hitting Miguel Rojas almost matched him, but Giants left fielder Turner Hill made a perfect throw to nab Edman in a close play at home to end the inning.
Betts’ and Smith’s bats stayed hot to open the sixth with a leadoff double and one-out RBI single, respectively. The Dodgers took advantage of the Giants’ sloppy infield play to load the bases for De Paula, who lined a two-run single into shallow center field.
Those were the kinds of stifling rallies that had defined the Dodgers offense earlier in the season, when they were scoring regularly in double digits.
The Dodgers’ 15 hits Saturday were their most in a game since July 2 against the San Diego Padres, and just two shy of their season high.
